findings.issue: part3.htn/part4.htn: the vocabulary is an invented ontology, and it is the rubric's own list of slop terms: holder, primer, guarded, exposed, open, vulnerable, blast/3, reacts/3, strike/2, mark/2, signature/2, and 'vantage' (takeVantage). Game words are renamed too: role(?e, enemy) or canAct instead of enemy/ally, connected instead of linked, and regionHas and skillElement stand in for terrain, hasTag and skillAppliesTag.
findings.fix: Use the game's words: ally(?a), enemy(?t), at, linked, hasSkill, skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), hasTag, immune, terrain. Delete holder, primer, guarded, exposed, open, vulnerable and signature. A skill is picked by the tag it applies.

findings.issue: part3.htn castElementAs, blastEntities, settleTerrain and sufferTerrain make up an effect engine. The planner simulates reactions (a feature rewrites into a new feature, the blast applies statuses, the terrain settles on whoever stands there) through allOf passes and opStatus. Nothing here states what makes a strategy possible.
findings.fix: Delete the chemistry simulator. Write each combo as a strategy whose if() names the tags it needs, e.g. if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), skillAppliesTag(?s1, wet), skillAppliesTag(?s2, electrocute), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)), with do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)).

findings.issue: ruleset.htn uses first(and(...)) here and at line 61. The same pattern is in part2.htn at lines 41, 48, 56 and 64, and in part3.htn at lines 47, 80, 114 and 122. `and` is not a built-in, so an undefined name is silently false. The two-hop move, takeVantage's move, lure, push, taunt, holder, castElementAs, strikeElement and markElement therefore never find a binding.
findings.fix: first() already takes a conjunction. Write first(hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)) without the and().

findings.issue: ruleset.htn navigate is a 1- and 2-hop ladder written with else. A target 3 regions away has no plan. takeVantage adds a third hand-rolled search over region/lineOfSight on top of it.
findings.fix: Use recursion with pathNext over linked/2: navigate(?a, ?to) :- else, if(at(?a, ?here), pathNext(?here, ?to, ?next)), do(opMoveTo(?a, ?here, ?next), navigate(?a, ?to)). Plan at room level and let the engine handle line of sight.

findings.issue: part4.htn: cooperation is threaded through a `?not` extra arity with a `none` sentinel (blastDeadAt/2, strikeDead/2, castElement/3, strikeElement/3). The distinct-actors requirement is buried in helpers instead of being stated in the strategy's if().
findings.fix: Bind both actors in the strategy's if() with ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2), then pass them to generic verbs like prepareToUseSkill(?a1, ?s, ?t) and useSkillOnTarget(?a1, ?s, ?t). Delete every ?not overload.

findings.issue: part3.htn: charges, signature, unlimited, free, canPay and payFor are resource bookkeeping, a level below what the game needs decisions at. Each cast verb repeats the same hasSkill/skillElement/canPay triple.
findings.fix: Remove the cost accounting. A skill is available if ally(?a) and hasSkill(?a, ?s). If learning a skill matters, give prepareToUseSkill two cases: already has it, or go learn it.

findings.issue: part2.htn lure, push and taunt each rebuild the actor search, takeVantage, payFor and try(sufferTerrain) inline. The lure method with else releases an anchored ally, which ties holdPosition's shield state into movement. opLure and opPush are the same operator.
findings.fix: Make one verb, bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l), with one method per way to move a mob, each gated by a skill tag (pull, push, dash) and not(immune(?t, ?tag)). Drop anchoring from this component.

findings.issue: Every file opens with an essay-length header: design rationale, GDD citations, links to .claude/rules, and schema lists of the invented predicates. Several method comments run to 3 or 4 lines and name level content (Warden, Magnetize, flare), which also breaks R8.
findings.fix: Keep a one-line header per file and one short line per method, e.g. '% Case 2: no ally has the skill - learn it first.' Remove the named characters and skills.

core_primitives.summary: This is an effect engine with an invented ontology: a chemistry simulator, role-exclusion sentinels, charge bookkeeping and a 2-hop navigation ladder, with no strategy that states its feasibility in if(). The undefined `and` inside first() also silently disables most of its methods.

findings.issue: The Wraith is modelled as an effect engine with made-up terms: behavior/4, effect/3 with remove()/grant()/spill(), reach/2, suspends/2, heavy/1, weakness/4, zoneReaction, receptive. The planner has to simulate the physics to find out what works. This is the ontology of the deleted core/abilities tree, which the owner rated slop.
findings.fix: Write the Wraith's weaknesses and reactions as plain game facts: skillAppliesTag(?s, blind), immune(wraith, forcedMove), hasTag(wraith, stealthed). Then write one method per winning strategy whose if() states those facts directly.

findings.issue: The win methods have empty or near-empty if()s. What makes each strategy possible (who has a flash or taunt, who can reveal, who can drown or drop the Wraith, two distinct allies) is hidden inside spend/reveal/iceOver/neutralize. You can't read an if() and say when a strategy works.
findings.fix: Write one strategy per method, like flashAndDrop(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), skillAppliesTag(?s1, blind), skillAppliesTag(?s2, forcedMove), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)), do(applyTag(blind, ?t), applyTag(forcedMove, ?t)). Then planToDefeat(?t) lists those strategies as its menu.

findings.issue: iceOver, spend, reveal, stepOut, stepAll, confirmTag and confirmOff are one-off helpers, and each is used by a single win line. These are the makeTrap/coverAt/finishTrap pattern. None of them is a reusable verb whose methods are the ways to reach a state.
findings.fix: Replace them with the generic verbs applyTag(?tag, ?t) and prepareToUseSkill/useSkillOnTarget. Give applyTag one method per way (a skill, a location such as the well, a terrain zone), as in gh_tag_application.

findings.issue: `first(and(canAct(?a), at(?a, ?r)))`: `and` is not a built-in and not defined, so it is silently false. The second stepOut method never applies, and the team can never leave the crypt before the soulfire.
findings.fix: Write `first(canAct(?a), at(?a, ?r))`: first() already takes a conjunction. Better, make leaving the danger area a navigate step that the strategy's do() asks for.

findings.issue: `stepOut(?e) :- if(), do().` is a maybe-walk: every plan branches into staying and leaving. aimFor (lines 165-167) searches every way to aim, and spend/reveal search every skill and tag through behavior/effect. The planner is searching a physics simulator instead of carrying out plans the author chose.
findings.fix: Delete the do-nothing alternative and the aim search. Each strategy decides where its actors stand and what they aim at, and states that in its if() and do().

findings.issue: The level file contains methods (win, iceOver, spend, reveal, aimFor, stepOut) and names specific skills in its design (blindingFlash, tidalWave, hook). A level should be facts plus a goal. The strategies belong in reusable components that pick skills by their properties.
findings.fix: Move the strategies into components/strategies with no level names in them, leave only facts and `goals(planToDefeat(wraith)).` in the level, and use skill properties (skillAppliesTag) instead of skill names.

findings.issue: A 58-line essay header walks through the state machine, the methods and the traps in prose. The prose restates what the code should say plainly.
findings.fix: Cut it to a one-line header saying what the file is, plus one short comment per method.

findings.issue: rooted + immune(forcedMove) + suspends(exhausted, forcedMove), and rank(boss) + mana: a rule system stacked on the tags. The planner has to derive whether it can move the Wraith at all.
findings.fix: Use tags alone. The exhausted strategy's if() needs hasTag(?t, exhausted), and a method sets exhausted through applyTag. There is no suspends/2 layer.

fsm_wraith.summary: An effect-engine level in the style of the deleted core tree: a made-up behavior/effect/spill vocabulary, feasibility hidden in one-off helpers, maybe-walks and an aim search. It also has a silently-false `and(...)` that disables leaving the crypt. It needs to be rewritten as tag facts plus a menu of strategies whose if() states feasibility.

findings.issue: theSlipstream's do() is an imperative script of one-off helpers (makeTrap, coverAt, bringTo, gatherIntoTrap, finishTrap). The feasibility is hidden inside trapSite/primer rather than stated in if(): who snares, who finishes, and what the enemy is not immune to. This is the rubric's own slop example.
findings.fix: Put the enemy, not(immune(?e, snare)), skillAppliesTag(?s, snare), the finisher skill and distinct allies (\==(?a1, ?a2)) in if(). Then do(applyTag(snare, ?e), applyTag(<finishing tag>, ?e)).

findings.issue: The ruleset uses an invented ontology: role/2, status/2, regionHas, blast/3, reacts/3, primer, signature/2, expose, trapSite, strikeDead, blastDeadAt. The primitives add exposed/guarded/open/holder/vantage. Each term is another thing the reader and the planner must learn.
findings.fix: Use the game's words instead: enemy/1, ally/1, at, linked, hasSkill, skillAppliesTag, immune, hasTag, terrain. Replace blast/reacts/primer with skillAppliesTag and tag facts.

findings.issue: makeTrap, coverAt, gatherIntoTrap, finishTrap and trapSite are each used by exactly one strategy. gatherOthers (ruleset.htn:18) duplicates gatherIntoTrap. There is no reusable verb whose methods are the ways to get a tag onto a target.
findings.fix: Write one applyTag(?tag, ?t) verb with one method per way: an ally skill, a location or terrain, or another mob's skill. Have both strategies call it, and delete the per-strategy helpers.

findings.issue: and(...) is not a built-in, so it is silently false. connected/2 is not the game's linked/2. The first coverAt method can never fire, and the else no-op at line 33 always runs, so the shield commitment described in the header never happens.
findings.fix: Drop coverAt. If cover matters, state it in if() as ally(?a), hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, shielded), linked(?edge, ?r), and call a generic verb.

findings.issue: Both finishTrap methods require status(?e, snared), but nothing in theSlipstream's if() or do() makes the enemy snared. Whether the plan works depends on a hidden side effect of bringTo/terrain in the primitives. The two alternatives also share an identical if(), so neither states what makes it possible.
findings.fix: Make snare an explicit state in do() (applyTag(snare, ?e)). Give each finish method its own feasibility, e.g. skillAppliesTag(?s, ?killTag) with not(immune(?e, ?killTag)).

findings.issue: The component encodes level mechanics: oil as a primer, sludge that persists, a shield-bearer, 'none' as a sentinel primer. It also picks actors by signature(?a, shield) (line 31), which selects a skill by name rather than by its properties.
findings.fix: Select skills by property (skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)) and actors by hasSkill. Move the terrain facts and oil/sludge specifics into the level file.

findings.issue: try(gatherOthers(...)) wraps an allOf, which fails if any single enemy can't be brought, so the whole gather is silently skipped. Also, once try succeeds it commits, so a gather that uses up a mover can make castElement or finishTrap fail without backtracking.
findings.fix: Drop the gather. If multi-target matters, use anyOf over enemies that can be brought, and state the needed movers in if() so the commit can't starve later steps.

findings.issue: The headers are design essays (roles, commitments, persistence across fights, 'one match, one fire') rather than a one-line file header plus one short line per method.
findings.fix: Use one header line ('the_burn: kill an enemy with a fire reaction on its terrain') and one line per method case.

core_upper.summary: This is the deleted core the_burn/the_slipstream shape: imperative chains of one-off helpers over an invented ontology (primer, reacts, blast, expose, signature), with feasibility hidden in helpers instead of if(). coverAt's and() is silently false, so the shield step never runs. The only sound part is defeatGroup as a menu (R5).

findings.issue: The goal `defeatEnemy` marks theSlipstream with `else`, so it is a fallback rather than an item on the menu. FindAllPlans never returns a Slipstream plan while theBurn works.
findings.fix: Drop `else`. Make both lines plain alternatives: `defeatEnemy(?e) :- if(enemy(?e), health(?e, healthy)), do(theBurn(?e)).` and `defeatEnemy(?e) :- if(enemy(?e), health(?e, healthy)), do(theSlipstream(?e)).`

findings.issue: theSlipstream freezes the room before the enemy arrives. triggerSnareEnemies (line 184) only snares enemies already in the room, and the `try` quietly skips it when there are none. The plan ends with the enemy standing on sludge, not snared, and it is still counted as a way to defeat the enemy.
findings.fix: Make being snared a state the strategy must reach: `do(bringEnemyTo(?lurer, ?e, ?oilRoom), applyTag(?freezer, frozen, ?oilRoom))`. Or give the frozen terrain a rule that snares whoever enters. Also, the Slipstream only disables the enemy, so it belongs under a disable goal, not `defeatEnemy`.

findings.issue: The `if()` picks the lurer because it can apply `magnetized`, but `do()` never uses that skill. bringEnemyTo is a walk-over-and-take-aggro lure that any ally could perform. The `if()` therefore states a need the plan does not have.
findings.fix: Either have bringEnemyTo use the pull skill (a method `bringEnemyTo` with `if(canApplyTag(?a, magnetized))` that casts it), or change the condition to `ally(?lurer)` and let bringEnemyTo's methods choose between the aggro lure and the magnetize pull.

findings.issue: applyTagEffect/triggerBurnOil/triggerBurnEnemies/triggerFreezeOil/triggerSnareEnemies form a small effect engine: reactions are chained through `try`, and the bespoke operators opFreezeOilIntoSludge and opInstakill are called from inside the tag verb. The reactions are hidden from the strategy, and each `try` can silently do nothing.
findings.fix: Keep the physics as data at the bottom, e.g. `reaction(burning, oil, none)` and `reaction(frozen, oil, frozenSludge)`. Use a single opApplyTag operator. Let the strategy's `do()` name the state it wants, e.g. `applyTag(?igniter, burning, ?oilRoom)`, then `defeated(?e)`, and have the methods test the reaction facts in `if()`.

findings.issue: Nothing guards the `add` calls in opApplyCondition (lines 108-109) or opGetAggro (lines 132-133). A second burn or freeze of the same room, snaring an enemy that is already snared, or luring twice raises an error that aborts the whole search. Aggro is also never released after the lure.
findings.fix: Guard with `not(condition(?loc, ?tag))` and `not(hasAggro(?a, ?e))` in the calling method's `if()`. Call opReleaseAggro at the end of bringEnemyTo.

findings.issue: This is dead or unused vocabulary: opWound, opKill, the healthy/bloodied/dead health ladder, and the facts `size/2`, `location/1`, `room/1`, `corridor/1`, `agent/1` and `opRemoveCondition`. It is stat bookkeeping and ontology that no method reads.
findings.fix: Delete the unused operators and facts. Use a single tag such as `hasTag(?e, dead)` in place of the three-step health ladder.

findings.issue: The header does not match the file. It says 8 Swarmers (there are 3), says the Warden 'pulls' with Magnetize (the code walks over and takes aggro), and names specific characters that the generic code never names.
findings.fix: Replace it with one line that says what the file is, and one short line per strategy that names its tags (lure onto oil, then burning; frozen oil, then lure in).

findings.issue: `at(?enemy, ?enemyLoc)` in both strategies binds a variable that `do()` never uses (bringEnemyTo looks it up again). Also, applyTag needs the caster to already be standing at the location, so every strategy has to add its own navigateTo before calling it.
findings.fix: Remove the unused `at/2` conditions. Give applyTag a second method, 'not there yet: navigateTo then apply', so strategies only list `applyTag(?who, ?tag, ?loc)`.

combatlevel1_greasetrap.summary: The architecture is right: skills are chosen by the tags they apply, the actors are distinct, the verbs are mostly generic, and the file is level facts plus a goal. But the goal uses `else` where it should offer a menu, the Slipstream never actually snares the enemy, the magnetize condition is decorative, and the tag effects are a small try-chained effect engine.

findings.issue: This is an effect engine. The ruleset contains no strategies. `applyAbility`, `applyEffect` and `effectOn` interpret `effect(?ab, recipient, atom)` data one atom at a time, so the planner has to simulate physics to find a combo. None of the `if()` clauses say when anything works.
findings.fix: Delete the interpreter. Write goal methods such as `defeat(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), skillAppliesTag(?s, wet), ...), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(shock, ?t))`, with one method per winning strategy and operators that apply the tag directly.

findings.issue: The vocabulary is invented: grant/remove/purge atoms, `moment`, the recipients `target|self|area|foes|around`, `locus`, `receptive`, `anchoredAgainst`, `leapable`, `dashEdge`/`blinkEdge`, `heldAgainst`, `spotted`, `trudge`, `regionAtom`, `onGrant`, `behavior` aims `source/self/here/there`, `zoneReaction`, `mustSurvive`. It also mixes `tag/2` and `has/2` for the same idea.
findings.fix: Keep to the game's words: `ally`, `enemy`, `at`, `linked`, `hasSkill`, `skillAppliesTag`, `immune`, `hasTag`, `terrain`. Add a predicate only when those can't express it.

findings.issue: `shove` has an unconditional `if(), do()` method, and the comment says every knockback aim is a plan. Push, pull, hook and pullIn are all searched as a physics simulator. The planner explores aims, and the author does not choose the plans.
findings.fix: Remove the simulated movement atoms. Where a strategy needs an enemy in a pit, write `bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l)` with one method per way to do it, chosen by `locationCanApplyTag(?l, ?tag)` in the strategy's `if()`.

findings.issue: `loseTrack` guards only `follows(?npc, ?src)`, but `opLoseTrack` also deletes `tag(?npc, taunted)`. The second method calls `opRemove(?src, ?npc, taunted)` with no guard at all. Because `effectOn(..., chase, ...)` on line 402 reaches this code without checking for a taunt, it can `del` a fact that doesn't exist, and that error aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard both methods with `tag(?npc, taunted)`, and add a third method `if(not(tag(?npc, taunted))), do()`. Better: remove the chase simulation.

findings.issue: A hand-written iterative-deepening route search (`hop/1`, `walkable/5`, `nextStep`), plus `linked/3`, `edge/3`, bridged gaps, plates and knockbacks. This plans at a level the engine should handle, and it reimplements `pathNext`.
findings.fix: Use `navigate` over `linked/2` with the built-in `pathNext` and plan at the room level. Leave pathing, knockback landing and plate timing to the game engine.

findings.issue: `opReact`, `opProvoked`, `opExploit`, `opFall` and `opKnock` are `del(), add()` trace markers for the simulator, not game actions. Real state changes go through `opGrant`, `opRemove`, `opNavigate` and `telegraph`, which this file never defines.
findings.fix: Give each operator one game action and its real effect, e.g. `opUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag))`. Drop the marker operators.

findings.issue: Each atom's method always succeeds by design ('one refused atom never cancels the rest'). Tens of no-op branches such as `suffer`, `dashTo`, `blink`, `swapPlaces`, `drag` and `openIfHeld` make every ability 'succeed' whether or not it did anything. Each helper exists for one atom, so none of them is a reusable verb.
findings.fix: Make a verb fail when its goal state can't be reached. Replace the per-atom helpers with a few verbs (`applyTag`, `prepareToUseSkill`, `bringMobToLocation`), each with one method per way to achieve it.

findings.issue: The header is a 112-line essay: a design spec, a mode semantics section (react/raw/bare), and design history about `else`. Inline comments run to three or four lines.
findings.fix: Cut it to one header line saying what the file is, plus one short line per method or case.

ab_effects.summary: A physics and effect interpreter with its own invented ontology, not an HTN ruleset. It has no strategies and no feasibility in any `if()`, and it searches simulated knockbacks, chases and zones. It is textbook slop by R1, R3 and R4.

findings.issue: part4.htn navigateTo is a 2-hop ladder: 'direct' then 'via one intermediate' under else. Any route of 3 or more rooms gives no plan. clearZone, escortTo, pushToTarget and reachThroughGate all depend on it, so every challenge fails on a real map. The methods count hops; they are not different ways to move.
findings.fix: Use the recursive form from language.md §6: a base case if(at(?a, ?to)), then else, if(at(?a, ?here), pathNext(?here, ?to, ?next)), do(opMoveTo(?a, ?here, ?next), navigateTo(?a, ?to)) over linked/2. Blocked rooms should be missing from linked, not checked as each hop is unrolled.

findings.issue: part3.htn escortTo repeats the hop ladder (single-hop, then two-hop through ?via), and so does part5.htn pushToTarget (one push, then two pushes). These are copies of navigation that stop at 2 steps, not ways to escort or push.
findings.fix: Make each one recursive on pathNext: escortTo(?npc, ?dest) calls navigateTo(?a, npc's room), opEscort one hop, then escortTo again. pushToTarget does one opPush per hop and recurses. Filter safe rooms with a rule on the next hop.

findings.issue: The six files use seven overlapping words for position and obstruction: at, npcAt, objectAt, blocked, blocker, gateBlocking and safeFor, plus connected instead of linked. Because of this the parts don't compose. navigateTo checks blocked(?dest), not gateBlocking, so a gated room is walkable, and reachThroughGate is never needed.
findings.fix: Use one at(?thing, ?room) for agents, NPCs and objects, and linked/2 for adjacency. A closed gate removes a linked fact and opening it adds the fact back, so navigation respects gates without special cases.

findings.issue: part2.htn: opApplyEffect makes an effect appear with no actor and no skill, and ruleset.htn: opEliminate removes any blocker just by arriving. Neither if() says what makes the action possible (who does it, which skill produces which tag, whether the target is immune). This is an effect engine, not a strategy.
findings.fix: Guard the verb with its feasibility, for example applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(immune(?t, ?tag))), do(prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)). Removing a blocker should call the verbs that achieve its weakness, not an opEliminate.

findings.issue: The constant 'agent' is hard-coded in removeBlocker, escortTo and pushToTarget. Reusable components shouldn't name the character; companions are interchangeable and chosen by the plan.
findings.fix: Bind the actor in if() with ally(?a) (and ally(?a2), \==(?a, ?a2) where two are needed), then pass ?a to navigateTo and the op.

findings.issue: part2.htn executeCombo unrolls a 3-step combo and then a 2-step combo under else. Both if()s require needsEffect for every step, so the 'already present' case of applyEffect can never be reached, and a combo whose first step is already on the target fails. not(comboStep(?e3, 3)) is global, not per target. needsEffect/hasEffect duplicate hasTag.
findings.fix: Write the sequence as its needs, e.g. do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)), or recurse over the steps in order. Use hasTag, and have applyTag's base case be if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)).

findings.issue: part5.htn opPush: the comment says the agent moves to objLoc, but the operator only moves the object, so the agent's position is wrong for the next step. The if() takes any neighbour as ?pushFrom rather than the opposite side, and never checks that the target is free.
findings.fix: Change the effect to del(at(?a, ?from)), del(at(?obj, ?objLoc)), add(at(?a, ?objLoc)), add(at(?obj, ?target)). State 'behind' as a fact such as opposite(?from, ?objLoc, ?target) in if(), along with not(at(?other, ?target)).

findings.issue: Every file has a signature(...) block for the linter plus header jargon ('Pressure-class', 'Insight-class'). This is noise in the domain. In part6.htn the at(?agent, ?cur) bindings bind ?cur and never use it.
findings.fix: Drop the signature facts and the class labels; keep one header line saying what the file is. Delete the unused at(?agent, ?cur) conditions.

challenges.summary: Each file is one small reusable verb, which is the right direction. But the methods count hops instead of being different ways to do the task, the vocabulary splits one idea into seven predicates so the parts don't compose, and the ops produce effects with no stated feasibility. Workable toy challenges with a bad navigation core.

findings.issue: stunAndBurn calls applyIce and applyFireball, which are never defined, with ?a1 and ?a2 unbound. The strategy can never produce a plan, and it names skills rather than the tags it needs.
findings.fix: Write it like wetAndElectrocute: `if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, stun)), not(immune(?t, burn)))`, `do(applyEffect(stun, ?t), applyEffect(burn, ?t), opInflictDamage(?t))`.

findings.issue: The strategies' if() checks only enemy(?t) and never says what makes them possible. wetAndElectrocute plans against electricityElemental even though that enemy has immune(electricityElemental, electrocute).
findings.fix: Add the feasibility conditions to if(): `not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))`, plus some source for each tag (a skill that applies it, or a location that has it).

findings.issue: castSkill dispatches on skill names (wet, electrocute) to one operator per skill (opCastWet, opCastElectrocute). Each new skill needs new rules, and skills are chosen by name rather than by their properties.
findings.fix: Add a property fact `skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)` and select with `if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?e))`. Use one generic operator, `opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag))`.

findings.issue: The cast operators (lines 84-87) and useLocationToApplyEffect (line 123) have no effect, so the tag never lands on the target. opInflictDamage then succeeds whether or not wet or electrocute was applied.
findings.fix: Make each way of applying a tag end in an operator that adds `hasTag(?t, ?tag)`, guarded with `not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))`. Let opInflictDamage's caller check `hasTag(?t, wet), hasTag(?t, electrocute)` in if().

findings.issue: castSpellToTarget, doCastSpellToTarget and doSetMana are dead code that nothing calls. They use mana arithmetic, their names lack the op prefix, and doCastSpellToTarget has two overlapping heads (lines 105-106).
findings.fix: Delete lines 46-50 and 90-109. If a cost matters, model it as a tag such as `exhausted(?a)`, not as mana bookkeeping.

findings.issue: The second goToSameLocation method does not exclude the case where both are already in the same place. Co-located actors therefore get two plans, one of which is a self-move opMoveTo(?a, X, X). opStayInLocation and opTargetAlreadyAggroed are no-op operators that pollute the plan.
findings.fix: Guard the move with `\==(?aOldLocation, ?tOldLocation)`. Make the base cases `do()` instead of calling no-op operators.

findings.issue: The level facts (actors, positions, skills, mana, immunities) share one file with the reusable verbs. The file also has commented-out actors and facts, and gob is declared as an agent.
findings.fix: Move the facts and the goal into a level file and keep only the strategies, verbs and operators here. Delete the commented-out facts.

findings.issue: Commented-out code (line 104, line 163) and an empty section header (lines 166-173) are left in. No method has a one-line comment saying what case it handles.
findings.fix: Delete the leftovers. Add one line per method, e.g. `% Case 2: bring the target to a location that has the tag.`

gamehack3.summary: The shape is right: planToDamage is a menu of strategies, applyEffect has one method per way to apply a tag, and bringMobToLocation uses aggro. But stunAndBurn cannot run, no strategy states its feasibility (immunity is ignored), skills are dispatched by name, and the cast operators have no effect, so tags are never tracked. Dead mana code adds clutter.

findings.issue: doWet/doElectrocute (and the copies doWet2/doElectrocute2 at 140-150) repeat the same two methods once per tag. Each strategy gets its own verb instead of sharing one verb whose methods are the ways to get a tag.
findings.fix: Replace them with one verb, applyTag(?tag, ?t). Give it one method per way: an ally casts a skill with skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), or the target is brought to a location that applies ?tag. Then wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t)), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)).

findings.issue: stunAndBurn picks skills by name (hasSkill(?a, ice), hasSkill(?a, fireball)), and hasSkill(companionE, electrocute) makes a skill's name the same as its tag. It never checks ally(?a) or immune(?t, stun/burn).
findings.fix: Name skills separately from the tags they apply: skillAppliesTag(frostBolt, stun), skillAppliesTag(fireball, burn). The if() becomes: enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, stun)), not(immune(?t, burn)), skillAppliesTag(?s1, stun), skillAppliesTag(?s2, burn), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2).

findings.issue: The file carries dead experiments: wetAndElectrocute2 (defined twice, at 70 and 129), 3 and 4, test_wetAndElectrocute, and ifCanApply/canApply/canApply2/canApply3/ifCanSkillApplyEffect/ifCanLocationApplyEffect. castice, castWet, castSpellToTarget and skillApplyEffect are never called.
findings.fix: Delete every variant. Keep one planToDamage menu, one method per strategy, and one applyTag verb.

findings.issue: doEffectTE is a Prolog rule with no if()/do(), not a method. When do() calls it as a task, there is no method or operator, so wetAndElectrocute3/4 silently never plan. doEffectLocation also binds ?a to any ally, with no check.
findings.fix: Delete doEffectTE and doEffectLocation. The applyTag verb's methods replace them.

findings.issue: The first takeAggro method runs doAggro without checking for an existing aggro fact, so a duplicate add aborts the whole search. The second method only removes the old aggro and never adds the new one. It is also called as takeAggro(?t, ?a), so the argument order is unclear.
findings.fix: Guarded cases: takeAggro(?m, ?a) :- if(aggro(?m, ?a)), do(). takeAggro(?m, ?a) :- if(aggro(?m, ?o), \==(?o, ?a)), do(opAggro(?m, ?o, ?a)). takeAggro(?m, ?a) :- if(not(aggro(?m, ?x))), do(opAggro(?m, ?a)). In the last two, opAggro deletes any old aggro fact and adds aggro(?m, ?a).

findings.issue: applyice, applyFireball, applyWet and applyElectrocute have no effect, so no tag is ever recorded. inflictDamage then assumes the combo happened. Operators also lack the op prefix (moveTo, aggroMoveTo, doSetMana).
findings.fix: Use one operator, opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). Guard it with not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) in the caller. Rename moveTo to opMoveTo, and give inflictDamage a guard: if(hasTag(?t, wet), hasTag(?t, electrocute), not(damaged(?t))).

findings.issue: Mana bookkeeping (hasMana, manaCost, is/-, doSetMana) is stat arithmetic that no strategy uses.
findings.fix: Remove the mana facts and castSpellToTarget. If casting has a precondition, express it as a tag or skill property (e.g. hasSkill plus being in the same room).

findings.issue: The level world (agents, rooms, immunities, commented-out companions) is in the same file as the strategies and verbs. The movement methods also teleport the ally across rooms without linked/pathNext.
findings.fix: Split the facts into a level file. Keep the domain generic, and move with a navigate(?who, ?to) verb over linked/2 (pathNext), not with a bare moveTo from one room to another.

gamehack.summary: The top is the right shape: planToDamage is a menu, and wetAndElectrocute lists the tags it needs. Below that, skills are chosen by name, the per-tag verbs are copy-pasted, dead variants are left in, operators have no effect, and takeAggro is broken.

findings.issue: The strategies' if() only says enemy(?t). What makes them possible is hidden inside applyTag. immune(electricityElemental, electrocute) (line 45) is never checked, so wetAndElectrocute plans against an electrocute-immune enemy. Nothing makes the two actors distinct either, so cooperation is never required.
findings.fix: State the feasibility in if(), as in stunAndSlowSkill: enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute)), skillAppliesTag(?s1, wet), skillAppliesTag(?s2, electrocute), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2). Then do() lists the tags to achieve.

findings.issue: Mana arithmetic (hasMana, manaCost, opSetMana) and effort bookkeeping (allyEffort, moveEffort, increaseEffort, opUpdateEffort, lines 66-75 and 195-211) are stat accounting. This is the TrunkThumper granularity that the rubric says is too fine for this game.
findings.fix: Delete mana and effort. useSkillOnTarget checks hasSkill and co-location, then calls opUseSkill. Leave costs to the game engine, or express them as tags (for example, exhausted).

findings.issue: opApplyTag adds hasTag(?t, ?tag) with no guard. waterSkill applies both wet and clean, so if the target already has clean, the add is an error that aborts the whole search. opInflictDamage (line 162) is also unguarded if damaged(?t) already holds.
findings.fix: Guard the anyOf method with if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))), and check not(damaged(?t)) in the strategy's if().

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobToApplyTag (line 184) are empty stubs. Two of the three ways in applyTagNotPresent return 'success' without the tag ever being applied, so those plans lie about the state.
findings.fix: Give each an operator that applies the tag: opUseLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) and opMobSkillAppliesTag(?m, ?s, ?t), each adding hasTag(?t, ?tag) and guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)).

findings.issue: stunAndBurn applies ice and fire, so the name contradicts the body. applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag (line 152) is an invented, unreadable name.
findings.fix: Either rename it to freezeAndBurn, or make it apply the stun tag. Rename applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag to applySkillTags.

findings.issue: Dead code: moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe and useSkillOnTargetSafe are never called. useSkillOnTargetSafe calls applySpellToTarget, which is undefined. The distance/3 facts (lines 39-43, including distance(inn, inn, 10)) are unused, and there are commented-out companions.
findings.fix: Delete the *Safe variants, the distance facts and the commented-out facts. Keep one path, prepareToUseSkill then useSkillOnTarget.

findings.issue: Level facts (agents, positions, skills, mana) share one file with the reusable verbs (applyTag, bringMobToLocation, aggroTarget).
findings.fix: Split the file: the world facts plus goals(planToDamage(...)) go in a level, and applyTag, the movement verbs and the aggro verbs go in components.

findings.issue: opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation and opTargetAlreadyAggroed are no-op operators that only pad the plan with bookkeeping. They are not game actions.
findings.fix: Make these base cases do(), with nothing to do, guarded by the positive condition: applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do().

gamehack4.summary: The shape is right: a menu of strategies, and an applyTag verb with one method per way. But the strategies' if() hides feasibility and ignores immunity, two of the three ways are empty stubs, and the file carries mana/effort arithmetic, dead *Safe code and an unguarded add that can abort the search.

findings.issue: Both strategies' if() says only enemy(?t). Nothing states what makes them possible: no immunity check, no skill or location that produces each tag, no distinct actors. stunAndBurn calls applyIce(?a1, ?t) and applyFireball(?a2, ?t) with ?a1 and ?a2 unbound, and no ally has ice or fireball, so the plan holds variables and no real caster. wetAndElectrocute plans electrocute on electricityElemental, which is immune to it.
findings.fix: Put the feasibility in if(): `enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute)), skillAppliesTag(?s, electrocute), ally(?a)`. Then do() should be only the states to reach: `do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t))`.

findings.issue: There is one hand-copied verb per tag (doWet, doElectrocute, doWet2, doElectrocute2, applyEffect, doEffectCast, skillApplyEffect, applySkill, castWet, castice, castSpellToTarget). The location method's 4-step body is pasted five times (lines 72, 79, 144, 169, 175). The right idea is here (a skill way and a location way to get a tag), but it isn't a single reusable verb.
findings.fix: Write one `applyTag(?tag, ?t)` with one method per way: `if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag))` then prepareToUseSkill and useSkillOnTarget; and `if(locationCanApplyTag(?l, ?tag))` then bringMobToLocation and useLocationToApplyTag. Delete the per-tag copies.

findings.issue: Skills are named after the tag they produce (hasSkill(companionW, wet)), so the skill and the effect are the same atom. Strategies then pick skills by name (applyIce, applyFireball, applySkill(?a, ?t, wet)), not by their properties.
findings.fix: Give skills their own names and properties: `hasSkill(companionW, splash)`, `skillAppliesTag(splash, wet)`. Choose skills in if() only through skillAppliesTag or skillHasTag.

findings.issue: doElectrocute's first method is `if()` with an unbound ?a. It always succeeds and emits applyElectrocute(?a, ?t) with no caster, no range and no immunity check, so every enemy gets a bogus electrocute plan.
findings.fix: Bind and check in if(): `ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, electrocute), hasSkill(?a, ?s), not(immune(?t, electrocute))`, then go to the target before casting.

findings.issue: takeAggro's first method adds aggro(?a, ?t) with no guard. If the enemy already has that aggro, the add is an error that aborts the whole search. The second method only removes the old aggro and never adds the new one. The call at line 73 is takeAggro(?t, ?a), so the argument roles are also muddled.
findings.fix: Write two exclusive cases: `if(not(aggro(?e, ?any)))` then opTakeAggro(?e, ?a); and `if(aggro(?e, ?old), \==(?old, ?a))` then opSwitchAggro(?e, ?old, ?a), which does del(aggro(?e, ?old)) and add(aggro(?e, ?a)).

findings.issue: ifCanApply and ifCanLocationApplyEffect use `!`, which is not a built-in here, so they are always false. wetAndElectrocute2, 3 and 4 can never plan. doEffectTE (line 140) is a Prolog rule, not a method, so do(doEffectTE(...)) finds no method and fails silently. static/1 is never defined.
findings.fix: Delete the cut variants, the numbered strategy copies and test_wetAndElectrocute. For one binding use first(...) inside if(). Write doEffectTE as `if(...), do(...)` methods, or remove it in favour of applyTag.

findings.issue: Operators are not named op*, and almost none has an effect. applyWet and applyElectrocute add nothing, so nothing records that the target is wet, and electrocute never depends on wet. There are duplicate operators: doCastSpellToTarget at lines 208-209 gives duplicate plans, and casticeOperator overlaps applyIce. doStayInLocation() is an empty no-op.
findings.fix: Have `opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)` add `hasTag(?t, ?tag)`. Guard it with `not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))` in the calling method, and make the damage step require hasTag(?t, wet). Give the already-there case of goToSameLocation an empty do().

findings.issue: castSpellToTarget does mana arithmetic (hasMana, manaCost, is/>=) that no strategy uses. This is stat bookkeeping below the level the game plans at, and it adds to the dead code (castice, castWet, canApply3, applyEffect). The file also mixes level facts with the domain.
findings.fix: Drop the mana, and gate skills with tags or preconditions if needed. Delete the unused helpers. Split the world facts (lines 1-48) into a level file, and keep the reusable verbs free of companionE/companionW specifics.

gamehack2.summary: Underneath this is the right idea: a menu of strategies, plus a skill way and a location way to get a tag. But the file is a pile of copied per-tag helpers and abandoned numbered variants. Strategies check only enemy(?t), and skills are named after their effects. Several parts can never work or give wrong plans: `!`, unbound casters, the unguarded aggro add, and operators with no effect.

findings.issue: The header says 'using else so that only one thing happens', but the first two doAI methods (lines 62, 64) are plain alternatives. attackKingAttackers and attackKing both return plans, and the else group only runs when both of them fail. The comment and the menu disagree.
findings.fix: Decide whether the goal is a menu or a priority list. For a priority list, mark line 64 `else` too. For a menu, change the comment to say the first two are alternatives and the rest are fallbacks.

findings.issue: attackUnit reuses ?Type, which line 111 already bound to the enemy's type. As a result a pawn can only capture pawns and a king can only capture kings, so a pawn next to the enemy king can never take it.
findings.fix: Use a fresh variable for the attacker, `unit(?Unit, ?AttackerType, ?Player)`, or drop the type with `unit(?Unit, ?_, ?Player)`.

findings.issue: The plain-move fallback is `else, if(at(?Unit, ?Current))`. Because else is not a cut, backtracking can re-enter it while the destination is occupied, and the plan then puts two units on one tile.
findings.fix: Guard the base case with the negation: `if(at(?Unit, ?Current), not(at(?Other, ?Destination)))`.

findings.issue: The operators captureUnit and doMove don't follow the op... naming, so the plan can't be told apart from the methods at a glance.
findings.fix: Rename them to opCapture(?unit, ?tile) and opMove(?unit, ?from, ?to).

findings.issue: opponent/2 is computed with ==, = and a cut, but it is a fixed fact of the world.
findings.fix: Replace it with two facts: `opponent(Player1, Player2). opponent(Player2, Player1).`

findings.issue: The world (tiles, units, positions) sits in the same file as the domain, so the strategies can't be reused on another board.
findings.fix: Move the tile/unit/at facts to a level or problem file and keep the methods, operators and axioms as the domain.

findings.issue: The header points to gettingstarted.md, which isn't part of the ruleset. The rule comments also restate each goal line ('Get its position').
findings.fix: Keep one line per method saying what it is for, and drop the per-goal narration and the external pointer.

game.summary: This is a clear teaching example. doAI is a short, prioritized menu of strategies built from reusable verbs (attackUnit, moveClosestPawnNearKing, tryMove), and the board geometry lives in plain axioms. The rough edges are the ?Type reuse bug in attackUnit, an else fallback that isn't guarded by a negation, and a priority comment that doesn't match how the methods are grouped.

findings.issue: The strategies' if() only says enemy(?t), so it does not state what makes them possible. wetAndElectrocute does not check not(immune(?t, electrocute)), so it plans against electricityElemental, which is immune (line 39). stunAndBurn plans ice with no ice skill in the world. Nothing checks immunity anywhere in the file.
findings.fix: Put the feasibility in if(): wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)). Do the same for stunAndBurn with ice and fire.

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobToApplyTag (line 156) are empty do() stubs. The location and mob routes never add hasTag, and they put no game action in the plan. The plan claims the target is wet, but the state never says so, and the engine has nothing to execute.
findings.fix: Make each one end in an operator that is a game action and adds the tag, for example opApplyTag(?tag, ?t) guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). The mob route should also check at(?m, ?l), at(?t, ?l).

findings.issue: The anyOf in applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag calls opApplyTag for every tag the skill has, with no guard. waterSkill adds both wet and clean, so if the target already has clean, add(hasTag(?t, clean)) is an error and aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the anyOf condition with if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))). Rename the task to something plain such as applySkillTags(?s, ?t).

findings.issue: The skill route only works if an ally already has the skill. canGetSkillAtLocation (lines 58-59) is declared but never used. The player has no skills, so the 'go learn it first' case is missing and the player can never be the actor.
findings.fix: Add a prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t) verb with two methods: the ally already has the skill (go to the target), or it doesn't (go to a location with canGetSkillAtLocation(?l, ?s), learn the skill with an operator, then go to the target). Call it from applyTagNotPresent.

findings.issue: Dead helpers: moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe, useSkillOnTargetSafe (which calls applySpellToTarget, never defined), and opAggroMoveTo's twin opMoveTo. The unused agent/1 and commented-out companion facts are clutter too. moveAndUseSkillOnTarget names its skill parameter ?tag.
findings.fix: Delete the *Safe variants, agent/1 and the commented-out facts. Keep one version of useSkillOnTarget, and name its parameter ?s.

findings.issue: opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation (line 174) and opTargetAlreadyAggroed (line 197) are empty operators that exist only as bookkeeping. They are not game actions, and they add noise to every plan.
findings.fix: Write those base cases as methods with an empty do(), for example applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do().

findings.issue: goToLocation teleports in one opMoveTo and ignores linked/2. It is marked only '% Unsafe', and when ?a is already at ?l it moves the actor from ?l to ?l.
findings.fix: Use the navigate pattern: a base case at(?a, ?l) with do(), then a recursive step over pathNext(?here, ?l, ?next) with opMoveTo.

findings.issue: The world facts (actors, rooms, skills) and the reusable verbs share one file, and the file has no header and no goal line.
findings.fix: Split the domain (applyTag, the strategies, movement, aggro) from the level facts. Add a one-line header and goals(planToDamage(...)).

gamehack5onlyplans.summary: This is the right GameHack architecture: a menu of strategies, a generic applyTag verb whose methods are the ways to apply a tag, and tags chosen by skill properties. But it is unfinished. The strategies check no immunity, the location and mob routes are empty stubs that never apply the tag, an unguarded add in the anyOf can abort the search, and dead *Safe helpers and no-op operators add noise.

findings.issue: Both ally methods call useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?tag, ?t), passing the tag where the skill belongs. applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag then asks skillAppliesTag(ice, ?tag), finds nothing, and falls into the empty second method. The plan says the ally used the skill, but hasTag is never added. The same bug is at line 96.
findings.fix: Pass the skill that if() found: useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t).

findings.issue: Neither strategy's if() says what makes it possible: it is only enemy(?t). immune(electricityElemental, electrocute) is declared but never checked, so wetAndElectrocute plans against an immune target. stunAndBurn also doesn't say which skills give the tags.
findings.fix: Put the feasibility in if(): wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)). Do the same for stunAndBurn.

findings.issue: The location and mob ways to apply a tag are stubs with do(). They 'succeed' without adding hasTag, so a plan can finish with the target still untagged. useMobSkillToApplyTag's head also says ?tag, but callers pass the skill ?s (line 104).
findings.fix: Give them operators that do the game action: useLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) :- if(not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))), do(opApplyTag(?tag, ?t)). Do the same for useMobSkillToApplyTag(?m, ?s, ?t), going through the skill's tags.

findings.issue: The anyOf adds every tag the skill applies, with no guard. waterSkill gives both wet and clean, so if the target already has clean, add(hasTag(?t, clean)) is an error and aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the binding: if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))). Rename the verb to plain words, e.g. applySkillTags(?s, ?t).

findings.issue: Dead and half-written verbs sit beside the live ones: moveAndUseSkillOnTarget (empty), moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe and useSkillOnTargetSafe (never called, and they call applySpellToTarget, which is undefined). useSkillOnTarget has an empty if(), so it never checks that the actor has the skill or is at the target.
findings.fix: Delete the unused variants. Keep one useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)), do(applySkillTags(?s, ?t)).

findings.issue: No-op operators (opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation, opTargetAlreadyAggroed) put steps into the plan that the game doesn't perform.
findings.fix: Write the base cases as do(), e.g. applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do().

findings.issue: stunAndBurn applies the tags ice and fire. The strategy name and the tags disagree, and the skill facts are iceSkill/fireballSkill while the commented hasSkill facts say ice/fireball.
findings.fix: Name the strategy by the tags it achieves (freezeAndBurn), or add a stun tag. Use one set of skill names.

findings.issue: The level facts (with commented-out companions and locations) live in the same file as the reusable verbs. goToSameLocation also duplicates goToLocation.
findings.fix: Move the facts and the goal to a level file. goToSameLocation(?a, ?t) :- if(at(?t, ?l)), do(goToLocation(?a, ?l)).

gamehack6swapskills.summary: The GameHack architecture is right: a strategy menu, an applyTag verb whose methods are the ways to apply a tag, and aggro to pull mobs. But the strategies don't check feasibility (immunity), the skill/tag argument mix-up means the ally path never tags anything, and the location/mob paths and several verbs are empty stubs or dead code.

findings.issue: wetAndElectrocute's if() checks only enemy(?t). It never says the target must not be immune to wet or electrocute, so it plans to electrocute electricityElemental, which is immune(electricityElemental, electrocute).
findings.fix: State what makes the strategy possible: if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), as stunAndSlowSkill does for stun.

findings.issue: not(immune(?t, ?slowSkill)) checks immunity against a skill name. immune/2 holds tags, so this check is always true.
findings.fix: not(immune(?t, slow)). Immunity is to the tag, never to the skill.

findings.issue: The skill case of applyTagNotPresent leaves ?a unbound. prepareToUseSkill then binds ?a through hasSkill(?a, ?s), so any skill holder, such as teslaTower, can become the caster.
findings.fix: Put the actor in if(): if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)).

findings.issue: opApplyTag does add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) with no guard. useSkillOnTarget has an empty if(), and the anyOf at line 172 does not check the tag. If the tag is already on the target, the add is an error that aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard it in the anyOf: if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))). Give useSkillOnTarget an if() that checks hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l).

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobSkillToApplyTag are empty stubs, so the location and mob routes never put the tag on the target. Also, useMobSkillToApplyTag's head names its second argument ?tag, but line 141 passes a skill.
findings.fix: Make each one call a game action that adds hasTag(?t, ?tag), guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). Name the arguments consistently: (?m, ?s, ?t).

findings.issue: opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation and opTargetAlreadyAggroed are 'nothing to do' base cases written as operators. They are not game actions, and they clutter every plan.
findings.fix: Write already-true cases as empty do(): applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do(). Do the same in goToLocation, goToSameLocation and aggroTarget.

findings.issue: The file carries dead and half-finished code: stunAndSlowSkillDebug, useSkillOnTargetSafe (it calls an undefined applySpellToTarget and tests hasTag against a skill), prepareToApplyTag (never called), and bringMobToLocation/3. The coined name applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag is jargon.
findings.fix: Delete the unused methods and rename the helper to a plain verb, such as applySkillTags(?s, ?t).

findings.issue: The level facts, including commented-out alternatives for companions and skills, share one file with the reusable verbs and strategies. The domain is tied to this one world.
findings.fix: Move the facts and the goal to a level file, and keep the strategies and verbs in components that name no specific characters, places or skills.

gamehack8agentattop.summary: The architecture is right: a menu of strategies, feasibility in if(), and reusable tag, skill and aggro verbs with one method per way. It is unfinished: wetAndElectrocute ignores immunity, one immunity check tests a skill instead of a tag, the caster can be unbound, opApplyTag's add is unguarded, stub methods never apply tags, and dead code and no-op operators remain.

findings.issue: `not(immune(?t, ?slowSkill))` tests immunity against a skill name, not a tag. Immunity is declared per tag, so this check is always true and a target immune to slow still gets this strategy.
findings.fix: Use `not(immune(?t, slow))`, the same way line 80 checks `stun`.

findings.issue: `useLocationToApplyTag` and `useMobSkillToApplyTag` (line 217) are empty stubs. The plan never adds `hasTag(?t, wet)` or `hasTag(?t, electrocute)`, and nothing appears for the game to execute. As a result, `wetAndElectrocute` succeeds without applying either tag. Line 139 also passes the skill `?s` into the `?tag` slot.
findings.fix: Make each stub call a game action, such as `opUseLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t)` or `opMobUsesSkill(?m, ?s, ?t)`, that adds `hasTag(?t, ?tag)` behind a `not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))` guard. Pass the tag and the skill in the correct argument positions.

findings.issue: The ally route's `if()` never states who acts. `?a` is first bound inside `prepareToUseSkill` by `hasSkill(?a, ?s)` (line 146), which also matches enemies, so `teslaTower` can be picked as the caster.
findings.fix: Put the actor in `if()`: `if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag))`. Also add `ally(?a)` to the first `prepareToUseSkill` case.

findings.issue: `opApplyTag` adds `hasTag(?t, ?tag)` without a guard. `useSkillOnTarget` has an empty `if()` (line 165), so a skill that applies a tag the target already has makes the add fail, and that error aborts the whole search. `useSkillOnTarget` also never checks that the caster has the skill or is in the same place as the target.
findings.fix: In `applySkillTags`, use `if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)))`. Give `useSkillOnTarget` the conditions that make the cast possible: `hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)`.

findings.issue: The file carries dead code. `stunAndSlowSkillDebug` has unbound actors. `useSkillOnTargetSafe` (line 155) calls an `applySpellToTarget` that does not exist and checks `hasTag(?t, ?s)` with a skill as the tag. `bringMobToLocation/3` (line 248) is an empty stub, and `opAggroMoveTo` duplicates `opMoveTo`.
findings.fix: Delete these, and keep one version of each verb.

findings.issue: No-op bookkeeping operators clutter the plan with steps that are not game actions: `opTagAlreadyOnTarget`, `opStayInLocation` (line 237) and `opTargetAlreadyAggroed` (line 261).
findings.fix: Write each 'already true' case as `if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do()`, and likewise for being in place or already aggroed. Keep only no-op operators the renderer needs, such as `opSynchronize`.

findings.issue: The `bringMobsTogether` methods overlap: when both mobs can move, cases 2 and 3 both apply, and cases 2 and 3 do not exclude the already-together case 1. The result is duplicate plans. `getSkillFromLocation` (line 186) also swaps out an arbitrary skill when an ally has several.
findings.fix: Make the cases exclusive. Add `\==(?l1, ?l2)` and `static(?m2)` to the case that moves `?m1`. For skills, pick the skill to replace explicitly, or give each ally one skill slot.

findings.issue: `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` is a coined name, not a game word. Level facts (lines 1-63) sit in the same file as the reusable verbs, with no header saying which part is which.
findings.fix: Rename it `applySkillTags(?s, ?t)`. Move the world facts into a level file and keep the strategies and verbs as a component (R8).

gamehack7combined.summary: The architecture is right: `planToDamage` is a menu of strategies, and `stunAndSlowSkill` and `wetAndElectrocute` state their needs through reusable verbs such as `applyTag` and `prepareToUseSkill`. It is unfinished, though: two tag-application routes are stubs that never apply the tag, `opApplyTag` is unguarded, the slow-immunity check tests the wrong thing, and dead debug code and no-op operators are left in.

findings.issue: Lines 5-35 declare a second ontology (`type(agent, ...)`, `type(location, ...)`, `type(tag, ...)`, `type(skill, ...)`) only for a linter. No method reads it, and it repeats what `ally`/`enemy`/`at`/`hasSkill`/`skillAppliesTag` already say. That is about 30 lines of scaffolding in a level that should be only the world.
findings.fix: Delete the `type/2` block. The linter can infer kinds from the component `signature/2` facts and the game facts. A level file is its facts plus its goal (R8).

findings.issue: No component uses `agent/1`, and it is inconsistent: it lists `gob` but leaves out the enemies `mimic`, `electricityElemental` and `teslaTower`. A reader can't tell what 'agent' means here.
findings.fix: Remove `agent/1`. `ally/1` and `enemy/1` are the game words that the strategies actually query.

findings.issue: No method queries `location/1`. Every location already appears in `at/2` or `locationCanApplyTag/2`, so these facts are dead vocabulary.
findings.fix: Delete the `location/1` facts, or add them only when a verb needs to list locations.

findings.issue: The goal `planToDamage(gob)` has a third method, `stunAndBurn`, but the level manifest doesn't depend on `gamehack/strategies/stun_and_burn`. That menu entry fails silently, as an undefined task, instead of failing because the world makes it impossible.
findings.fix: Add `stun_and_burn` to the level's dependencies, so every strategy on the menu is loaded and is ruled out by the world's facts (no stun/ice/fire skill), not by a missing file.

findings.issue: The level declares `immune(electricityElemental, electrocute)`, but the dependency `wetAndElectrocute(?t)` only checks `enemy(?t)` in `if()`. Pointed at `electricityElemental`, it would plan to electrocute an immune target. The world fact is ignored where it matters.
findings.fix: In the strategy, state what makes it possible: `if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute)))`.

findings.issue: The header says stun/slow is ruled out because there are no stun/slow skills. In fact the dependency `stunAndSlowSkill` queries `skillHasTag`, which nothing defines, so that strategy can never hold in any world. The level is 'correct' by accident.
findings.fix: In `stun_and_slow_skill`, use `skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow)`. The level's lack of stun/slow skills then really is what rules the strategy out.

findings.issue: The header records how the level was designed ('GH4-style', 'Only wetAndElectrocute strategy viable'). It doesn't say what the puzzle is: two routes to each tag (companion skill, or the lake plus the static tesla tower).
findings.fix: Use one line that says what the world offers, e.g. `% GH4: wet by companion or lake, electrocute by companion or the static tesla tower at the lake.`

gamehack_gh4.summary: The level has the right shape (world facts plus a goal, running on the GameHack verbs), and the lake plus static tesla tower gives the puzzle real alternative routes. It carries dead scaffolding (`type/2`, `agent/1`, `location/1`) and relies on a goal menu with an unloaded strategy and an unguarded immunity.

findings.issue: The world is trivial. One ally holds both skills and already stands next to the only enemy, so wetAndElectrocute gives a single plan that one actor finishes alone. The level asks the planner to decide nothing: no movement, no second ally, no choice between strategies.
findings.fix: Add a second ally and split the skills between them (hasSkill(player, waterSkill), hasSkill(ally2, lightningSkill)). Put the enemy in another location, and add skills with the properties that stunAndSlowSkill needs, so the goal's menu offers more than one real plan.

findings.issue: The type/2 block (lines 6-23) is linter scaffolding that repeats the world a second time. type(agent, ...) repeats agent/1 and ally/enemy, and type(location, room) repeats location/1. type(tag, ice) and type(tag, fire) name tags that nothing in this world produces.
findings.fix: Delete the type/2 block. The facts ally/enemy/at/hasSkill/skillAppliesTag already are the world. If the linter needs types, derive them from those facts in one place instead of listing them in every level.

findings.issue: agent/1 and location/1 add vocabulary that no strategy or verb in the loaded components reads. ally/1, enemy/1 and at/2 already say who and where everyone is.
findings.fix: Remove agent(...) and location(...), and keep only the game words the components query: ally, enemy, at, hasSkill, skillAppliesTag.

findings.issue: The header is test and design commentary ('Exercises applyTag -> applyTagNotPresent path 1', '... backtracks to wetAndElectrocute'), not a statement of what the level is. It is also wrong: planToDamage is a menu of plain alternatives, so nothing backtracks. stunAndSlowSkill just gives no plan.
findings.fix: Replace lines 1-4 with one line, e.g. '% GameHack MVP: one ally with water and lightning, one goblin in the same room.'

findings.issue: The comment depends on stunAndSlowSkill failing because skillHasTag(?, slow) is missing, but the level uses skillAppliesTag. The dependency uses two predicates for one property, so the reason that strategy fails here is a vocabulary mismatch, not the world.
findings.fix: Use skillAppliesTag everywhere in the strategy's if(), so the level fails or succeeds on its facts (no skill applies slow or stun), not on a misspelled predicate.

findings.issue: goals(planToDamage(gob)) calls a goal whose methods reach stunAndSlowSkill and stunAndBurn, but the level's manifest loads only wet_and_electrocute. Two of the three menu entries are undefined here and fail silently.
findings.fix: Add stun_and_slow_skill and stun_and_burn to the level's dependencies so the whole menu is loaded, and let the world's facts decide which strategies produce plans.

gamehack_mvp.summary: The shape is correct: a level made only of facts plus a goal, with no level specifics leaking into components. But the world is trivial: one ally solos a single plan. Linter type scaffolding, unused agent/location facts and a test-narrative header make it bloated.

findings.issue: The fireball's slow is written as skillHasTag(fireballSkill, slow), but its fire is skillAppliesTag. That gives two predicates for one idea, what a skill puts on a target. useSkillOnTarget only applies skillAppliesTag tags, so the check found 21 plans and none puts slow on gob. stunAndSlowSkill's slow is chosen in if() and then never achieved.
findings.fix: Write skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, slow) next to skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, fire), and drop skillHasTag from the vocabulary so the strategy selects its slow skill with skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow).

findings.issue: Lines 5-38 are 30 type/2 facts kept only for the linter. That is a third of the level, and it adds a second vocabulary (type(agent,_), type(location,_), type(tag,_), type(skill,_)) that no method reads. It also lists tags (ice, clean) and entities that play no part in the level.
findings.fix: Delete the type/2 block. A level is the world facts plus its goal. Let the linter infer kinds from ally/enemy/at/skillAppliesTag, or put its declarations in the component signatures.

findings.issue: agent/1 and location/1 (lines 41-44 and 64-70) are dead facts that no component reads. They also disagree with the world: agent(gob) is listed, but mimic, electricityElemental and teslaTower are not, even though they are enemies with positions.
findings.fix: Delete agent/1 and location/1. ally/1, enemy/1 and at/2 already say who exists and where.

findings.issue: The header claims 'companionF: fireball' as the slow half of stunAndSlowSkill, and 'Both ... viable'. But slow is never applied (see line 84). The goal's third strategy, stunAndBurn, needs a skill that applies ice, and this world has none, so the menu option fails without any note.
findings.fix: Use a one-line header that says what the world is (two allies, a lake that makes things wet, a static lightning tower), and make the facts match what it claims.

findings.issue: mimic, electricityElemental with immune(electricityElemental, electrocute), and volcano as a skill source appear to be copied from another GH level. None of them touches planToDamage(gob), so they add noise without adding any choice.
findings.fix: Remove the entities the goal never uses. Or make a distractor count: for example, put gob somewhere the tower can't be brought, so immunity and static matter.

findings.issue: Every ally can learn every skill at no cost, and the allies start with the two needed skills. So stunAndSlowSkill returns every ordered ally pair, including companions who swap away the skills they already have (plan 1: companionI trades iceBlast for fireball while player learns iceBlast). That makes 21 near-duplicate plans, not distinct strategies.
findings.fix: Keep the skill sources that create a real decision (sea for waterSkill). Drop mountain and volcano, which only re-teach skills the allies already hold.

gamehack_gh7.summary: It is a level of the right shape: world facts and a goal built on the GameHack components. But a third of it is linter scaffolding and dead vocabulary (type/2, agent/1, location/1). skillHasTag splits the skill-tag vocabulary in two, so the slow that stunAndSlowSkill promises is never applied.

findings.issue: part5.htn: `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` runs `opApplyTag` for every tag the skill applies, and nothing checks whether the target already has that tag. `useSkillOnTarget` and `useMobSkillToApplyTag` both reach this path without a guard. A multi-tag skill used on a target that already has one of its tags, or a stun strategy on a target that is already stunned, adds a fact that already exists. That error aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the anyOf method with `if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)))`. Better still, have it call `applyTag(?tag, ?t)`, which already handles the tag being present or absent.

findings.issue: part2.htn: `unlockDoor` synchronizes two allies on two plates but never moves them there. The plates' locations are missing from `if()`, and `do()` has no `goToLocation`. The unordered choice of plates and allies also returns the same plan four times: (p1,p2) × (a1,a2).
findings.fix: In `if()`, bind `at(?p1, ?l1), at(?p2, ?l2)`. In `do()`, call `goToLocation(?a1, ?l1), goToLocation(?a2, ?l2)` and then the sync operator. To break the symmetry, order the plates, or give each plate fact a role.

findings.issue: The already-done cases are operators with no effect: `opTargetAlreadyAggroed` (ruleset.htn:20), `opStayInLocation` (part3.htn:20) and `opTagAlreadyOnTarget` (part5.htn:21). They are not game actions and they clutter every plan with bookkeeping steps.
findings.fix: Make each base case `do()` (e.g. `goToLocation(?a, ?l) :- if(at(?a, ?l)), do().`) and delete these operators. Keep only real markers such as `opSynchronize`.

findings.issue: part5.htn: `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` is a coined name that exposes an implementation detail. It is not a plain game verb.
findings.fix: Rename it `applySkillTags(?s, ?t)`. Its methods would be 'apply each tag the skill has' and 'the skill has no tags'.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn: `bringMobsTogether` methods 2 and 3 don't exclude method 1 or each other. When the two mobs already share a location, all three give an empty plan, and when both can move, both movers are offered. The result is duplicate plans.
findings.fix: Add `at(?m1, ?l1), at(?m2, ?l2), \==(?l1, ?l2)` to methods 2 and 3 so that each method is a distinct way.

findings.issue: part3.htn: `goToSameLocation` checks `not(static(?a))`, but `goToLocation` does not. So `bringMobToLocation` and `prepareToUseSkill` can move a static entity. `bringMobToLocation` also binds `at(?a, ?aOldLocation)` (ruleset.htn:36) and never uses it.
findings.fix: Put `not(static(?a))` in the moving case of `goToLocation` and drop the unused `at(?a, ?aOldLocation)`.

findings.issue: part2.htn: the header and operator comments describe runtime internals ('SynchroLens', 'lens carries plate positions', 'Pure marker operator'), which is design notes rather than what the method is for.
findings.fix: Cut them to one line each, e.g. `% Two allies stand on the door's two plates at once.`

findings.issue: Every file declares `signature/2` linter metadata inside the domain. It is one more predicate for the reader and the planner that the game does not use.
findings.fix: Move the type signatures to the component manifest or a linter sidecar, so the .htn holds only the domain.

gh_primitives.summary: The architecture is right: reusable verbs (`applyTag`, `prepareToUseSkill`, `bringMobToLocation`), and each verb's methods are the ways to achieve it. But the multi-tag skill path has an unguarded `add` that can abort the search. The door primitive also skips moving the allies to the plates, and effect-free bookkeeping operators clutter the plans.

findings.issue: Slow is written with a second predicate, `skillHasTag`, and not with `skillAppliesTag`. `useSkillOnTarget` applies only `skillAppliesTag` tags, so the stun-and-slow plan casts fireballSkill and gives gob `fire`, never `slow`. The strategy reports success, but the state it names is never reached.
findings.fix: Write `skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, slow).` and change stunAndSlowSkill's if() to `skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow)`, so one plain game word covers every tag a skill produces.

findings.issue: The header lists test coverage ("all three damage strategies", "dispatcher paths exercised", "returns many distinct plans"), not the world. Line 101 names a component's internal precondition ("unlocks stunAndSlowSkill precondition"), which ties the level's facts to one strategy's implementation.
findings.fix: Use one header line that describes the world, e.g. `% Arena: gob with the party; a tesla tower at the lake shore, an ice elemental on the glacier.` Give each section a plain label, e.g. `% Skill tags`.

findings.issue: The level aims for plan count, not distinct strategies. Four interchangeable allies, two wet locations (lakeShore, sea), and waterSkill both held and learnable multiply each strategy into many plans that differ only by who or where. FindAllPlans no longer reads as a menu of strategies.
findings.fix: Keep one source for each way to get a tag: one ally skill, one wet location, one skill-bearing mob. Then each plan is a different strategy or way (ally skill / location / mob), not a different actor permutation.

findings.issue: Every entity is declared three times: `type(agent, X)`, `agent(X)`, and `ally/enemy(X)`, and every location twice. That is 30+ lines of bookkeeping that the reader must keep in sync with the real facts.
findings.fix: Keep `ally`, `enemy`, `at` and `locationCanApplyTag` as the world. Derive the rest with rules: `agent(?x) :- ally(?x).` `agent(?x) :- enemy(?x).` `type(agent, ?x) :- agent(?x).`, and the same for locations. Or drop the linter-only `type` facts.

findings.issue: The tag `clean` (declared here, produced by waterSkill at line 95) is used by no strategy and no weakness. It is vocabulary the planner and reader must carry for nothing. The same goes for `sea` (line 71), a wet location nobody stands in or needs.
findings.fix: Delete `type(tag, clean)`, `skillAppliesTag(waterSkill, clean)` and the `sea` facts, unless an immunity or strategy uses them.

findings.issue: teslaTower and iceElemental are declared `enemy` only so that they act as skill-bearing mobs, but that also makes them valid planToDamage targets. Their role in the level is a tag source, and nothing states that.
findings.fix: If they are hazards and not foes, drop `enemy` and rely on `hasSkill` plus `not(ally(?m))`, which path 3 already requires. Otherwise keep them, and give them immunities so that damaging them is a real puzzle.

gamehack_multipath.summary: The shape is right: the level is only facts plus a goal, uses the component vocabulary, and names nothing inside the components. But the fireball fact uses a second predicate (`skillHasTag`), so stun-and-slow never actually applies slow, and the file is padded with triple declarations, test-coverage comments and redundant sources that inflate the plan count without adding strategies.

findings.issue: part5.htn: the reusable goal completeToyLevel hard-codes door1 and gob1. Its first two methods also repeat the locked/unlocked split that unlockDoor already handles with its own no-op case.
findings.fix: Pass the door and enemy as parameters, e.g. completeLevel(?d, ?t) :- if(enemy(?t)), do(unlockDoor(?d), planToDamage(?t)). Keep door1 and gob1 in the level's facts and goal, and drop the duplicated locked/not(locked) methods.

findings.issue: part4.htn: wetAndElectrocute's if() checks only enemy(?t). It never rules out immune(?t, wet) or immune(?t, electrocute). Levels gh4 and gh7 declare immune(electricityElemental, electrocute), so this strategy returns a plan against an immune enemy. stunAndBurn (part2.htn:10) and applyTagNotPresent path 1 (ruleset.htn:10) have the same gap.
findings.fix: State the immunities in if(): if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))). Do the same for ice/fire in stunAndBurn.

findings.issue: part3.htn: stunAndSlowSkill calls useSkillOnTarget directly and skips applyTag's hasTag guard. useSkillOnTarget ends in opApplyTag, whose add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) is an error if the target is already stunned or slowed, and that error aborts the whole search rather than just this branch.
findings.fix: Add not(hasTag(?t, stun)) and not(hasTag(?t, slow)) to the strategy's if().

findings.issue: part3.htn: skillHasTag(?slowSkill, slow) is a second predicate for the same fact as skillAppliesTag. Levels must now declare both (gh7 and multipath do). A level that declares only skillAppliesTag silently loses this strategy, as the gamehack_mvp comment shows.
findings.fix: Use skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow) and delete skillHasTag from the vocabulary.

findings.issue: part3.htn: stunAndSlowSkill hand-rolls skill use and does not go through the shared tag verb. It cannot use the location or non-ally-mob ways to apply stun/slow that applyTagNotPresent offers, so it is less general than its sequential siblings.
findings.fix: Keep the synchronized skill use, since it is the point of the strategy. Choose skills by property in if() and add the hasTag guards so the only thing that differs from applyTag is the timing.

findings.issue: part2.htn: the header is design history ('documented failure', 'declared in GH1-GH6 but never had the required skills'). The name stunAndBurn says stun, but the strategy applies ice.
findings.fix: Use a one-line header such as '% freeze_and_burn - apply ice, then fire'. Rename the task to match the tags it applies.

findings.issue: part3.htn: opSynchronize is defined inside one strategy file, but it is a generic game action that any simultaneous strategy needs.
findings.fix: Move opSynchronize into a shared primitive (for example gh_movement) so other strategies can reuse it.

findings.issue: part6.htn: the comment says planToDamage 'tries stunAndSlowSkill first, then wetAndElectrocute', but the methods are plain alternatives and FindAllPlans returns all of them. The comment also leaves out stunAndBurn.
findings.fix: Replace it with '% Menu of damage strategies; one plan per strategy that works.'

gh_upper.summary: The architecture is right: a menu goal, sequential strategies built from a reusable applyTag verb whose methods are the three ways to apply a tag, and skills chosen by tag. The rough edges are a level-specific goal component, immunities missing from if() (so plans are made against immune enemies), an unguarded opApplyTag in stunAndSlowSkill, and a duplicate skillHasTag predicate.

findings.issue: The world is written in the deleted core's invented chemistry: reacts/3, blast/3, hazard/2, strike/2 and mark/2. The rubric lists these by name as slop. They turn the level into input data for an effect engine instead of stating the game's facts.
findings.fix: State what each skill does with skillAppliesTag(ignite, burn) and friends. Give enemies weaknesses and immune/2 facts. Say what the ground does with terrain(corridor, oil) and locationCanApplyTag(corridor, burn), so the strategies call applyTag(burn, ?t) instead of searching a reaction table.

findings.issue: signature/2 repeats hasSkill/2 for the same pairs, and the core strategies use it to pick a companion by name ('the Warden plants the shield'). That makes it a skill kind and a role marker at once.
findings.fix: Delete signature/2. Strategies choose an ally by the skill's property, e.g. hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, block).

findings.issue: role(player, player) and role(_, companion) give the player a special status. Companions are interchangeable and differ only in who controls them. role/2 also stands in for the game words ally/enemy.
findings.fix: Use ally(player). ally(warden). ally(arcanist). enemy(swarm). enemy(bearer). Cooperation should come from distinct actors in if() (\==(?a1, ?a2)), not from role(player).

findings.issue: unlimited/1 and charge(player, ignite, i1) are bookkeeping for ammunition tokens, which is too fine-grained for the decisions this game makes. skillElement(dash, dash) and skillElement(flare, light) are elements with no meaning.
findings.fix: Drop the charges and the unlimited facts. If a skill can be used only once, make that a tag or state that the operator consumes. Map dash to what it does: skillAppliesTag(dash, push).

findings.issue: Rooms use connected/2 and regionHas/2 instead of the game words linked/2 (which the built-in pathNext reads) and terrain. lineOfSight/2 adds a third graph that no strategy states it needs.
findings.fix: Write linked(entry, corridor) etc. and terrain(corridor, oil). Remove lineOfSight unless a strategy's if() requires it.
