findings.issue: The 22-line header is an essay. It narrates both strategies step by step, names which companion does what, and includes a design hypothesis with fun-metric targets.
findings.fix: Cut it to one line that says what the level is, e.g. '% Grease Trap: oiled corridor, a swarm in the gallery, an iron bearer at the exit.' Move the hypothesis to the level's design notes.

findings.issue: The goal is fine as a level goal, but it depends on core's defeatGroup, whose strategies (theBurn, theSlipstream) are scripts of one-off helpers (makeTrap, coverAt, gatherIntoTrap, finishTrap). The level inherits their slop.
findings.fix: Build the goal on a menu of generic strategies (e.g. defeatEnemy(?t) with one method per way to kill, each built from applyTag and bringMobToLocation) and keep this file to facts plus clearGreaseTrap.

findings.issue: The names defeatGroup and funBlocker tie the goal to the core vocabulary. 'Group' is not a game concept here, because each blocker is a single enemy fact.
findings.fix: Name the goal verb defeatEnemy(?t) and point funBlockerGoal at it.

grease_trap.summary: The level has the right shape (facts plus a goal), but its whole vocabulary is the deleted core ontology (reacts/blast/strike/mark/signature/role/charge), which the rubric calls slop, and it has an essay header. It needs rewriting into ally/enemy/linked/terrain/skillAppliesTag/immune facts that sit on top of generic strategies.

findings.issue: The goal `win` is one fixed script: `bringTo(ogre, brink, none), stepBack, finish(ogre)`. Its `if()` is empty, so nothing says when a ring-out works: no enemy, no verge area, no skill that moves or knocks, no two distinct actors. The feasibility is hidden inside the core helpers `bringTo`, `knockOn` and `confirmStopped`, which do not exist in this repo and came from the deleted slop tree.
findings.fix: State the strategy's needs in `if()`, for example `ringOut(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), hasTag(?edge, verge), skillAppliesTag(?pull, pull), skillAppliesTag(?push, knockback), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2))`. Then write `do()` as generic verbs: `do(applyTag(pull, ?t), applyTag(knockback, ?t))`.

findings.issue: The goal is not a menu. The four ways to bring the ogre (hook, taunt) and knock it over (fireball, bash, wave, vortex) are described only in the header essay. They are not separate strategies, so FindAllPlans cannot return one plan per strategy.
findings.fix: Write one `ringOut` method per winning strategy, such as pull-then-knock and lure-then-knock. Put the different ways to move a mob into the methods of a reusable `bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l)` verb.

findings.issue: `stepBack` is a maybe-walk. Its empty method always succeeds, and a second method optionally walks everyone off the brink, so every plan is doubled. `allBack`, `onBrink` and `finish` are one-off helpers that no other strategy uses. The planner is searching a physics simulator instead of the author choosing the plans.
findings.fix: Delete `stepBack`, `allBack` and `onBrink`. If a strategy needs an actor to leave the edge, make that a step of that strategy's `do()` using the shared movement verb (`navigate(?a, ?safe)`).

findings.issue: The file uses an invented ontology: `behavior(ogre, taunted, groundSlam, here)`, `feature(brink, verge, chasm)`, `knockOn(?e, feature(verge), none)`, `neutralized`, `confirmStopped`, `canAct`, `gone` and `forbidden(?a, move)`. The planner and the reader must learn each of these terms, and they encode an effect engine (slam windows, stuns, sacrifices).
findings.fix: Use the game's words: `enemy(ogre)`, `at(ogre, plinth)`, `hasTag(brink, verge)`, `skillAppliesTag(hook, pull)`, `skillAppliesTag(fireball, knockback)`. Drop the slam and stun simulation (R7).

findings.issue: `role(player, player)` versus `role(mage, companion)`, and `role(ogre, enemy)`, give actors roles by who controls them. Companions are interchangeable, and cooperation should come from the strategy's two distinct actors.
findings.fix: Write `ally(player). ally(mage). enemy(ogre).`, and require `ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)` in the strategy's `if()`.

findings.issue: The map uses `region/1` and one-way `connected/2`, plus nine hand-written `lineOfSight/2` facts. The built-in `pathNext` works over `linked/2`, so this vocabulary needs its own navigation code. Line of sight is detail the engine should resolve.
findings.fix: Declare the map as `linked/2` facts in both directions and navigate with `pathNext`. Drop `lineOfSight`, or reduce range to a property such as `skillRange(?s, adjacent)` only if a strategy's `if()` needs it.

findings.issue: The 27-line header is an essay. It gives the design history (Into the Breach), the slam physics, the traps and the sacrifice rules. The code does not express this logic.
findings.fix: Reduce the header to one line: `% Ring-Out: push the ogre off the brink's verge.`. Add one short comment per strategy method.

findings.issue: `mana(player, 4)` and `mana(mage, 4)` are stat bookkeeping, and nothing in this file uses them.
findings.fix: Delete the mana facts. Plan with tags and skill properties, not resource arithmetic.

movement_ringout.summary: This is a level whose goal is an imperative script over deleted core helpers. It has an empty `if()`, a maybe-walk `stepBack`, an invented slam and verge ontology, and a header essay that describes strategies the code never states as a menu. It is slop in the core-tree style, not a list of feasibility conditions followed by generic verbs.

findings.issue: The file has no methods, operators or goal. It is a fixture of facts only, so there is no strategy or plan to judge, and nothing calls pathNext from a task.
findings.fix: Add the idiomatic verb from language.md section 6: `navigate(?who, ?to) :- if(at(?who, ?to)), do().` and `navigate(?who, ?to) :- else, if(at(?who, ?here), pathNext(?here, ?to, ?next)), do(opMoveTo(?who, ?here, ?next), navigate(?who, ?to)).`, with `opMoveTo` doing `del(at(?who, ?from)), add(at(?who, ?to))`, an `at(hero, roomNW).` fact and `goals(navigate(hero, roomSE)).`

findings.issue: The `size/2` facts are labelled 'movement cost', but pathNext finds the shortest route by counting hops over linked/2 and never reads size. The data is dead, and the comment suggests weighted pathfinding that doesn't happen.
findings.fix: Delete the size facts. If cost matters, leave it to the engine, since planning happens at room level, not at the level of distances.

findings.issue: The 'should find shortest path' expectation is ambiguous. roomNW to roomSE has two routes of equal length, one through corridorN and one through corridorW, so the expected first hop isn't stated. The test queries are also plain comments, so nothing runs or checks them.
findings.fix: Write them in the doctest form `% ?: pathNext(roomNW, roomSE, ?next).` with `% => ?next = ...` lines, which pins down the tie-break, or assert them in a goals()/test harness.

findings.issue: The header says this is a test for a built-in, yet it sits in a ruleset position. The ASCII map is fine, but nothing says what the file is for as a domain.
findings.fix: Keep the one-line header and the map. Once the navigate task exists, add one comment line per method (base case: already there; recursive case: take the first hop).

pathtest.summary: This is a topology fixture: symmetric linked/2 facts and no tasks, so there is nothing wrong in its design, but there is also nothing to plan. The unused 'movement cost' sizes and the unchecked comment queries mislead the reader.

findings.issue: do_ai is a one-step reactive priority list (walk to boss, else press 'button', else walk to the button). It is not a decomposition toward a goal. On this level it returns only o_move(player, a0, a1): the plan never presses the button or reaches the boss.
findings.fix: Start from the need. reachBoss(?a) :- if(enemy(?e), at(?e, ?r)), do(navigate(?a, ?r)). Then give navigate a second way through a closed door: if(linked(?x, ?y), door(?x, ?y, ?d), closed(?d), opens(?b, ?d)), do(openDoor(?b, ?d), navigate(?a, ?r)), where openDoor(?b, ?d) has one method for each way to open it.

findings.issue: The file hand-rolls reachability with connected/3 (the door encoded as the third argument), connected_1, connected_2, free_connected and not_member over nested pairs. That is invented vocabulary, and the built-in pathNext over linked/2 already does this job.
findings.fix: Use linked(a0, a1)-style facts plus door(a2, a3, d0) and closed(d0), and navigate with the language.md pattern: a base case at(?who, ?to), then pathNext and opMoveTo per hop. Delete connected_1, connected_2, free_connected and not_member.

findings.issue: The strategies name level objects: 'boss' on line 61 and 'button' on lines 62-63. The level facts (lines 1-31) sit in the same file as the domain, so nothing here can be reused.
findings.fix: Select by properties: enemy(?e), opens(?b, ?d). Move area, connected, location and button_connection into a level file that holds only facts and the goal.

findings.issue: The top task is an else-chain of single actions, not a menu of strategies. Line 62 has an empty if(), so it states nothing about when the strategy works. The else also only fires after 'go to boss' fails, and it hides why that failed (the door).
findings.fix: Make the goal plain alternatives, one per strategy (e.g. reach directly / open the door, then reach). Each if() states what makes the strategy possible.

findings.issue: trigger_button binds any connected(?loc1, ?loc2, ?d) for the door. The door is only a label on an edge, so 'this button opens a closed door between these rooms' is never stated as a condition. ?location is a singleton-looking join the linter flags.
findings.fix: Write openDoor(?a, ?d) :- if(opens(?b, ?d), closed(?d), at(?b, ?r)), do(navigate(?a, ?r), opPressButton(?a, ?b, ?d)), with opPressButton doing del(closed(?d)), add(open(?d)).

findings.issue: Cooperation is absent. The ruleset takes one ?actor, and the companion is never used, although the natural puzzle is one ally holding the button while another goes through.
findings.fix: Declare actors as ally(player) and ally(companion). Add a strategy whose if() picks two distinct allies (\==(?a1, ?a2)): ?a1 opens the door, ?a2 reaches the enemy.

findings.issue: The operators are named o_move and o_trigger_button instead of op.... o_move jumps across several rooms in one action, and o_trigger_button rewrites graph edges instead of changing door state.
findings.fix: Use opMoveTo(?who, ?from, ?to) for each linked hop, and opPressButton, which changes only closed(?d) to open(?d).

findings.issue: There is no header and no per-method comment, so the intent of each else case in do_ai has to be reverse-engineered.
findings.fix: Add a one-line file header and one line per method, e.g. '% Case 2: door closed - open it, then go through.'

jam.summary: It compiles, but it is a one-step reactive policy, not a plan. It hard-codes 'boss' and 'button', hand-rolls reachability with invented connected_1/connected_2/not_member instead of pathNext over linked/2, and never uses the companion. It needs a top-down rewrite: a navigate verb, an openDoor verb chosen by opens/closed properties, and a menu of strategies for reaching the enemy.

findings.issue: moveTo is a navigation ladder. It has a pathThrough/3 recursion, but nothing defines pathThrough, so that method is always silently false. Below it are hard-coded 2-hop and 3-hop methods that stop at 3 rooms and can bounce back and forth (via2 = current). It also uses connected/2 rather than linked/2.
findings.fix: Use two methods: `moveTo(?e,?to) :- if(at(?e,?to)), do().` and `moveTo(?e,?to) :- else, if(at(?e,?here), pathNext(?here,?to,?next)), do(opMoveTo(?e,?here,?next), moveTo(?e,?to)).` Rename connected to linked, and delete the pathThrough, 2-hop and 3-hop methods, plus reachable/canReach/connectedBoth.

findings.issue: enemyFollows ends with an `else, if(), do()` no-op. else is not a cut: when moveTo fails (the room can't be reached), the planner backtracks into that no-op. lureToRoom then returns a plan in which the enemy never reached the room.
findings.fix: Guard the no-op with the negation of its condition, `if(not(hasAggro(?enemy, ?target)))`, or drop it, so an enemy that can't follow makes the lure fail.

findings.issue: The Case 3 fallback of applyTag is an unguarded `else, if()`. If Case 1 or Case 2 is re-entered by backtracking, the planner can add hasTag(?entity, ?tag) when the entity already has it, or apply the raw tag alongside a tag it should have combined with. Adding a fact that already exists is an error, and an error aborts the whole search. Case 1 also adds ?result without checking that the entity doesn't already have it.
findings.fix: Guard Case 3 with `if(not(hasTag(?entity, ?tag)), not(hasTag(?entity, ?x), tagCombines(?tag, ?x, ?r)))`. Add `not(hasTag(?entity, ?result))` to Case 1's if().

findings.issue: The aggro primitive hard-codes the character `player`. opGetAggro/opLoseAggro only work for `player`, while enemyFollows takes a ?target. Companions are interchangeable, so a reusable component must not name an actor.
findings.fix: Parameterize by actor: `opGetAggro(?enemy, ?a) :- del(), add(hasAggro(?enemy, ?a)).`, `getAggro(?enemy, ?a)`, and `lureToRoom(?a, ?enemy, ?room)` with `ally(?a)` in its if().

findings.issue: getAggro, loseAggro and removeTag use `else, if(), do()` base cases. They are mutually exclusive in intent but not guarded, so backtracking re-enters the no-op and a plan can skip the work.
findings.fix: Write each base case as the negated condition, e.g. `getAggro(?e) :- if(hasAggro(?e, player)), do().` and `removeTag(?e,?t) :- if(not(hasTag(?e,?t))), do().`

findings.issue: lureToRoom's if() binds ?currentRoom and never uses it. It doesn't state what makes the lure possible: that the target is an enemy, that it can reach the room, or that it isn't already there.
findings.fix: `if(enemy(?enemy), ally(?a), at(?enemy, ?er), \==(?er, ?room))`, then `do(moveTo(?a, ?room), getAggro(?enemy, ?a), enemyFollows(?enemy, ?a))`.

findings.issue: The file has dead query helpers that add vocabulary: isAggressive, isFollowingPlayer, isVulnerableTo, which introduces `vulnerability` where the game word is `immune`, and hasAnyTag. The linter-only signature/2 facts add noise.
findings.fix: Delete the unused helpers. Use immune/2 when a strategy needs to check a weakness, and move the signature facts into the manifest or the linter config.

findings.issue: The reaction table in a generic tags primitive includes specific pairs, `electronics`/`disabled`, that belong to a particular level's objects rather than to the core tag physics.
findings.fix: Keep only the core reactions (wet/burning/electrified/frozen) in the primitive. Put object-specific reactions in the level's facts.

old_primitives.summary: The primitives have the right shape: small generic verbs, operators with one effect each, and tags instead of stats. But movement is a broken 2- and 3-hop ladder, several `else` no-ops let plans skip work, and the aggro component hard-codes `player`.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:15 and part2.htn:25/35 and part4.htn:14/23/30 name specific characters: canApplyTag(player, burning), canApplyTag(arcanist, frozen). Companions are interchangeable, so a reusable strategy must not know who 'player' or 'arcanist' is. freezeCorridor/igniteRoom also have no actor, so nobody casts the freeze or the fire.
findings.fix: Bind the actor in if(): ally(?a), canApplyTag(?a, burning). Pass ?a into the verbs, e.g. lureToRoom(?a, ?enemy, ?oilRoom), applyTagToRoom(?a, ?corridor, frozen).

findings.issue: part2.htn:58 applyTagToRoom uses `else, if()` as the case that calls opApplyRoomTag. When the room already has the tag and a later task fails, the planner backtracks into this else and adds a fact that already exists. That is an error, and it aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the operator case with the negation: applyTagToRoom(?room, ?tag) :- if(not(roomHasTag(?room, ?tag))), do(opApplyRoomTag(?room, ?tag)).

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:35 falls back to igniteRoom with `else`, which only consumes the oil. Else is not a cut, so if applyTag or a later step fails, theBurn still 'succeeds' by burning the oil with nobody in it. The enemy is never burned. part2.htn:73 (applyHazardEffect no-op) and ruleset.htn:51 (consumeHazard no-op) skip work the same way.
findings.fix: Remove the no-op else branches. igniteRoom should require the enemy in the room: if(roomHasHazard(?room, oil), at(?enemy, ?room)). consumeHazard's base case should be if(not(roomHasHazard(?room, ?h))), do().

findings.issue: part4.htn:19 makes defeatEnemy an else chain instead of a menu, so FindAllPlans never returns theBurn and theSlipstream together. Strategy 3 (line 28) pushes the enemy into any hazard without checking it is vulnerable, so it is not a strategy. The goal also repeats each strategy's preconditions.
findings.fix: Use plain alternatives: defeatEnemy(?e) :- if(enemy(?e)), do(theBurn(?e)). and defeatEnemy(?e) :- if(enemy(?e)), do(theSlipstream(?e)). Drop strategy 3, and let each strategy's if() own its feasibility.

findings.issue: part2.htn:21 theSlipstream's if() never checks that the enemy is vulnerable to the hazard's tag (only defeatEnemy does), so the strategy alone doesn't say when it works. The 'simpler version' at line 31 is a second path shape hidden behind else, and ?enemyRoom in ruleset.htn:20 is bound but unused.
findings.fix: Put hazardAppliesTag(?hazard, ?tag), vulnerableTo(?enemy, ?tag) in theSlipstream's if(). Leave the route to a navigation verb rather than two else-ordered methods for 'corridor' and 'adjacent'.

findings.issue: part2.htn:43 freezeCorridor and :48 freezeRoom are identical one-off wrappers around applyTagToRoom. They are used only by theSlipstream, and they re-check canApplyTag(arcanist, frozen).
findings.fix: Delete both. Call the generic verb applyTagToRoom(?a, ?room, frozen) directly from theSlipstream.

findings.issue: part2.htn:63 pushIntoRoom moves the enemy straight to ?hazardRoom with opMoveTo, with no adjacency check and no pusher. In the corridor case it teleports two hops. The locomotion it depends on also uses hand-written 2- and 3-hop connected ladders instead of pathNext.
findings.fix: Have an ally push the enemy one hop at a time over linked/2 with pathNext, e.g. pushTo(?a, ?enemy, ?room) with a base case at(?enemy, ?room).

findings.issue: The signature/2 blocks (ruleset.htn:6-9, part2.htn:6-12, part3.htn:6, part4.htn:6) are linter scaffolding in the domain. The files also mix overlapping state words: roomHasHazard, roomHasTag, hazardConsumed, isEnemy vs enemy, and vulnerableTo vs immune.
findings.fix: Drop the signature facts. Use one room-state predicate (a tag on the location, as in hasTag) and the standard enemy/immune vocabulary.

old_upper.summary: The architecture is right: primitives, strategies and a goal layer, with theBurn as 'oil room + someone can burn → lure, ignite'. But the strategies name specific characters, defeatEnemy is an else chain rather than a menu, and several `else, if()` fallbacks either skip the actual damage or can add a duplicate fact and abort the search.

findings.issue: Only the taxi method has a comment. The walk and bus methods of travel-to have none, and the file has no header saying what the domain is.
findings.fix: Add a one-line header, e.g. '% Taxi: get to a place by walking, taxi or bus, paying the fare.', and one short line above each travel-to method: '% Walk when it is close enough.', '% Bus on a route from here.'

findings.issue: The operators (hail, wait-for, ride, set-cash, walk) don't use the op prefix, so a reader can't tell at a glance which tasks are game actions and which are methods.
findings.fix: Rename them opHail, opWaitFor, opRide, opSetCash and opWalk (or op-hail and so on, to match the hyphenated style).

findings.issue: The taxi's 1.5 base fare is written in two places: in the have-taxi-fare rule (line 1) and as the pay-driver argument +(1.50, ?d). The feasibility check and the payment can drift apart.
findings.fix: Add a taxi-fare(?d, ?fare) rule. Use it in the if() as taxi-fare(?d, ?fare), have-cash(?m), >=(?m, ?fare), then call do(... pay-driver(?fare)).

taxi.summary: Every travel-to method's if() states what makes that way of travelling possible, and its do() is a few game actions. The goal is a menu of strategies, and the operator effects are guarded. What's left is naming and comment polish: this could be a teaching example.

findings.issue: The operators (`hail`, `wait-for`, `ride`, `set-cash`, `walk`) have no `op` prefix, so in `do()` they look the same as compound tasks like `pay-driver`.
findings.fix: Rename them `opHail`, `opWaitFor`, `opRide`, `opSetCash` and `opWalk`, so a reader can tell game actions from verbs.

findings.issue: The bus strategy's `if()` does not say that the person can pay the fare. The cash check is hidden inside `pay-driver`, so the `if()` alone doesn't tell you when the bus is possible. The taxi strategy does state it (`have-taxi-fare`).
findings.fix: Add `have-cash(?m), >=(?m, 1.00)` or a `have-bus-fare` rule to the bus method's `if()`, next to `bus-route`.

findings.issue: `distance/3` is one-way (downtown to X) and has no symmetric rule, so `travel-to(downtown)` from park, uptown or suburb only finds a plan if the person is already there.
findings.fix: Add `distance(?u, ?v, ?d) :- distance-fact(?v, ?u, ?d)` (or state both directions), so the world is symmetric and the strategies work from any location.

findings.issue: The file has no header saying what it is, and only the taxi method has a comment. The walk and bus methods have none.
findings.fix: Add a one-line header and one short line per `travel-to` method, e.g. `% Walk if close enough`, `% Take a taxi if we can afford it`, `% Take the bus on a route`.

taxi2.summary: This is the gold Taxi example. The only change is that the person is now `at(person, ?x)`, which makes `at/2` the same for people and vehicles and is if anything clearer. `travel-to` is a clean menu of strategies whose `if()` states when each works; what remains are the small rough edges of the original.

findings.issue: defeatAllGuards lists the level's rooms (clearRoom(storage), clearRoom(corridor)) when it should cover every enemy. A guard placed in main or generator is silently ignored, and the task name is written for this one level.
findings.fix: State the goal over the world: `defeatAll :- allOf, if(enemy(?e)), do(defeatEnemy(?e)).` The level then holds only facts plus `goals(...)`.

findings.issue: The level must name its characters `player` and `arcanist` because the_burn requires canApplyTag(player, burning) and the_slipstream requires canApplyTag(arcanist, frozen). Components are hard-coded to specific characters, and companions are not interchangeable.
findings.fix: Give characters skills that carry properties: `ally(player). hasSkill(player, ignite). skillAppliesTag(ignite, burning).` Strategies then bind `ally(?a), hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, burning)` in if().

findings.issue: The world uses coined predicates (isEnemy, roomHasHazard, canApplyTag, vulnerableTo) where the game vocabulary already has words. canApplyTag goes from character straight to tag and skips the skill.
findings.fix: Use the game words: enemy(guard1), terrain(storage, oil), hasSkill/skillAppliesTag, and not(immune(?t, ?tag)) instead of a separate vulnerableTo list.

findings.issue: The corridor-generator link was added only so slipstream finds a plan (the comment says so). The level's geometry is being bent to fit one strategy's hop rules. Also, arcanist has no at() fact and never moves, and warden has no ability, so the slipstream plan freezes rooms from nowhere and the second companion plays no part.
findings.fix: Place every ally with at(). Let the strategy's if() require the caster, e.g. `ally(?a), hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, frozen)`, and bring them there with a verb like `prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?room)`. Keep links that are true to the map.

findings.issue: Travel runs on locomotion's else-ladder: a direct link, then pathThrough (never defined, so always false), then fixed 2-hop and 3-hop methods. After theBurn the player is in storage, and reaching exit needs exactly the 3-hop case, so any longer route fails silently. slipstream's first method also relies on the undefined pathThrough, so it never fires.
findings.fix: Replace moveTo's ladder with the recursive `pathNext` navigate over `linked/2` facts (language.md section 6), and rename connected/2 to linked/2 in the level.

findings.issue: The goal reaches strategy choice through defeatEnemy, whose strategies are chained with `else`. Once theBurn works, slipstream is never offered, so there is one plan per enemy rather than a menu. The strategy 3 fallback also ignores vulnerability.
findings.fix: Make defeatEnemy's methods plain alternatives, each guarded by what makes it possible (not(immune(?e, burning)), terrain(?r, oil), ...). Drop the vulnerability-blind fallback.

findings.issue: Nothing in the plan ever makes a guard defeated. theBurn only adds hasTag(guard1, burning), and completePuzzle never checks that the enemies are down. vulnerableTo is used only to pick a strategy, so 'defeat' is never a state the plan achieves.
findings.fix: Have the strategy's do() end in the achieved state, e.g. applyTag(?e, ?weakness) where a weakness means defeated. Make the goal's if()/base case test not(enemy(?e), not(defeated(?e))).

findings.issue: About 30 lines of type(...) declarations exist only for a linter. They duplicate oil/electricity as both tag and hazard and declare hazards (fire, spikes, acid) and tags (wet) that the level never uses.
findings.fix: Delete the type block, or keep only the types the level uses. One header line is enough.

puzzle1.summary: Most of the level is facts plus a goal, the right overall shape. But the goal is written around named rooms and named characters, the old components' character-bound, else-chained strategies force its vocabulary and even its map links, and nothing ever makes an enemy defeated.

findings.issue: 'Beat the slam' and 'Take the slam' are scripts of seven operators each (opTaunt, opChase, opWindUp, opKnockOver, opMiss/opSlam). What makes each strategy work is only in the order of the steps, and none of the steps is a verb that other code uses. Strategy 2 even calls opKnockOver directly instead of going through knockOver.
findings.fix: Make each strategy's do() a list of states to reach: ringOut(?e) :- if(enemy(?e), verge(?r), ...), do(bringMobToLocation(?e, ?r), knockOver(?e, ?r)). Put the hook, the taunt and the slam timing inside the methods of those verbs.

findings.issue: There is no reusable verb for 'get the enemy onto the brink'. The hook and the taunt are two ways to reach the same state, but they are written as separate top-level strategies, and strategies 2 and 3 repeat the navigate/taunt/chase/wind-up prefix.
findings.fix: Add bringMobToLocation(?e, ?r) with one method per way: one for a skill that pulls (hook), one for a skill that taunts, where the ogre follows the taunter. The strategies then differ only in which methods get chosen.

findings.issue: The planner scripts the ogre's own AI, frame by frame: opChase, opWindUp, then opMiss or opSlam, with a groundSlam constant. This is an effect engine for telegraph timing, which is the game engine's job, not a planning decision.
findings.fix: Collapse this to the state the companions choose. For example, the taunt method of bringMobToLocation adds at(?e, ?r) and aggro(?e, ?t). Model 'the taunter is stunned' as a tag (hasTag(?t, stunned)) that one taunt method adds, not as a chain of wind-up, miss and slam operators.

findings.issue: Skills are chosen by name (knows(?h, hook), knows(?t, taunt)), and the level's places are hard-coded in the methods: plinth and brink (lines 139, 146-157), brink/verge/yard in knockOver (lines 163-171), and ogre in win (line 133).
findings.fix: Choose skills by their properties, e.g. skillAppliesTag(?s, pull) and skillAppliesTag(?s, taunt). Bind places from facts in if(): at(?e, ?from), verge(?r), and a place next to it for stepping off. Write win as if(enemy(?e)), do(ringOut(?e)).

findings.issue: The if() does not say who the actors are or why a ring-out applies. companion/1 and enemy/1 are declared but never checked. Nothing states that the ogre can't be hurt, or which place has the verge: verge(brink, verge) is never used, and location/1 is dead data.
findings.fix: Add companion(?h), companion(?k), \==(?h, ?k), enemy(?e) and verge(?r) to the if(), and use ?r everywhere brink is hard-coded now. Delete location/1 and the unused second argument of verge.

findings.issue: knockFrom/2 mixes skill range with this level's map: fireball is cast from the gate and shieldBash from the yard. first(knockFrom(...)) hides that the value comes from a lookup table. The terms push/sweep and the verge constant are coined words on top of this.
findings.fix: Give skills generic properties, such as skillAppliesTag(fireball, knockback) and skillHasTag(tidalWave, area). Derive where to cast from with a rule over linked/2 or a 'sees' fact, not a table keyed by skill name.

findings.issue: The file header is a 38-line essay: an ASCII map, a restatement of each strategy, the expected plan set per kit, and design history ('rewritten'). The comments on strategies 2 and 3 are also multi-line narration.
findings.fix: Use a one-line header, e.g. '% Ring-out: knock an unkillable enemy over a verge.', and one short line per method. Move the plan-set table into a test (assert_plan_set).

findings.issue: knockOver dispatches on push or sweep, which is good, but the sweep methods move the friend with navigateTo(?friend, yard) and knock the stunned friend over as a hard-coded second step. These are side effects, not states the method achieves.
findings.fix: Put 'the friend is off the verge' in a verb, e.g. clearArea(?r, ?friend), with a method for 'can walk away' and a method for 'stunned: it is lost'. The sweep method then becomes do(clearArea(?r, ?friend), useSkillOnTarget(?k, ?s, ?e)).

ringout.summary: The knockOver dispatch and the navigation are sound, but the strategies are imperative scripts that also simulate the ogre's turn-by-turn behaviour. Skills are chosen by name and the level's places are hard-coded throughout, with no reusable bring-the-enemy-to-the-verge verb.

findings.issue: theQuietRun and theLoudRun (159) are imperative scripts: stash bag, cut power, slip in, open, haul / scout, set, blow, storm, smash, grab. They list actions to perform, not states to achieve. Each of the 11 helpers (prepBag, killLights, getInside, openUp, carryOut, scoutExit, placeCharge, detonate, stormBreach, crackVault, takeLoot) is used by exactly one strategy.
findings.fix: Write each route as the states it needs, using shared generic verbs: theQuietRun(?v) :- if(...), do(disable(power), enter(?a2, ?v), open(?v), take(?a1, loot)). theLoudRun reuses enter/open/take and only differs in how the vault gets opened (a second method of open(?v)).

findings.issue: The if() does not say when the strategy works. It checks hasCutter(player) and cleared(alarm), but the other things it needs (a companion with a rope, an actor to carry the loot) are hidden in the helpers' conditions at lines 144-154. No actors are bound or kept distinct.
findings.fix: Move the feasibility into the strategy: if(cleared(alarm), ally(?a1), hasTool(?a1, cutter), ally(?a2), hasTool(?a2, rope), \==(?a1, ?a2)), then pass ?a1 and ?a2 into generic verbs in do().

findings.issue: Every helper method hardcodes an actor (player, companionA, companionB), one method per character, and detonate (173) is fixed to the player. That is role(player) under another name. Companions are interchangeable, so these methods cannot be reused and do not scale with the cast.
findings.fix: Replace the per-character clauses with one clause per way to do it, and bind the actor by capability: placeCharge(?a, ?v) :- if(ally(?a), hasTool(?a, charge)), do(opSetCharge(?a)).

findings.issue: A new predicate is invented for each item and each intermediate state: hasCutter, hasRope, hasCharge, hasHammer, bagReady, exitScouted, powerOff, breach, stormed, vaultOpen, doorOpen, usable, vaultSite, alarmed, blocker. The tools are dispatched by name, not by their properties.
findings.fix: Use one ownership predicate and one property predicate, for example hasTool(?a, ?tool) and toolDoes(?tool, cut/climb/blast/smash), mirroring hasSkill and skillAppliesTag. Express the states as tags on things, for example hasTag(vault, open) and hasTag(power, off).

findings.issue: Some alternatives are fake. detonate's second clause does the same thing as its first, with an irrelevant extra condition, so it duplicates plans. killLights clause 2 (142) needs hasCutter(companionA), which is never true. carryOut clause 2 (152) checks companionA's bag but has the player haul. placeCharge clause 3 (169) sets the charge with a hammer. These exist to inflate the choice metrics, not to model distinct ways to do the job.
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate, dead and nonsensical clauses. Give a verb a second method only when it is a genuinely different way to reach the state.

findings.issue: The 28-line header essay and the inline comments (81-83, 91-94, 109-112, 116-119, 139-140, 171-172) explain fun metrics (F1-F6, insight_depth, fingerprint depth, the GDD) and design intent. They do not say what each method is for.
findings.fix: Cut the header to one line saying what the level is. Give each method or case a single line, such as '% Quiet run: disable the power, sneak in, open from inside.'

findings.issue: The operators ignore their actor argument (opCutPower(?a) only adds powerOff, and opBlow, opSetCharge, opOpenFromWithin and opSmashVault do the same). No operator deletes anything, so nothing is used up and no actor's position changes, which makes 'inside' and 'stormed' meaningless flags. opStashBag and opScoutExit are setup moves that change nothing any rule needs except a later metric-bait check.
findings.fix: Have the operators change the real state: movement is del(at(?a, ?from)), add(at(?a, vault)), and opening is add(hasTag(vault, open)). Drop setup operators that exist only to delay a payoff, or make them a real precondition of a later step in its if().

findings.issue: In clear/1, usable/2 only reads carrying(player, ...), so only the player's kit counts. Then the else fallback (124) is a cut-like 'if there is no companion' that backtracking re-enters whenever a later route fails.
findings.fix: usable(?a, ?tool, ?b) :- ally(?a), carrying(?a, ?tool), defeats(?tool, ?b). Write clear(?b) as a single method that binds the actor in if(), and drop the else branch; if you keep two cases, guard the second with not(companion(?c)).

reference_good.summary: The top-level menu (runHeist) and the tool-versus-blocker clear/defeats check are reasonable. Both routes, though, are imperative scripts of single-use helpers with hardcoded characters, an invented predicate per item and state, and clauses padded to inflate the choice metrics, all under an essay header.

findings.issue: The header is a 50-line essay covering the port history, the chapter mapping, divergences and plan listings. The navigation block (223-231) and the doTrunkSlam block (267-279) are also design essays rather than one line per method.
findings.fix: Cut the header to one line saying what the file is, then give each method or case one short line, e.g. '% Case 2: trunk broken - fetch a fresh one, then attack.'

findings.issue: trunkHealth, powerUp and stamina are counters with decrease/increase and threshold checks (>=(?s, 4), >=(?p, 3)). This is stat arithmetic, which is too fine-grained for this game's level of decision.
findings.fix: Replace the counters with tags such as hasTag(?t, charged), hasTag(?t, tired) and hasTag(?t, brokenTrunk). Operators add or remove the tag, and the if() tests it.

findings.issue: The type/signature block adds a second vocabulary (type/2, signature/2) that the planner never reads. The reader has to learn it, and it is noise in a domain file.
findings.fix: Move the type hints to a separate linter file, or drop them.

findings.issue: inMeleeRange(?t, ?e) is a static fact, yet the strategy navigates to the enemy afterwards. The feasibility condition does not match what do() achieves, because being in range is the state that navigateTo produces.
findings.fix: Drop inMeleeRange from if(); navigateTo(?t, ?loc) is the verb that achieves being in range.

findings.issue: at(?e, ?loc) binds ?loc, but do() never uses it. It is a dead condition in the Boulder toss strategy.
findings.fix: Remove at(?e, ?loc), or use it for a real range requirement.

findings.issue: opRecovery increases stamina with no cap. Chained plans can push stamina above its maximum, so the stamina gates in the strategies lose their meaning.
findings.fix: Model recovery as removing a tired tag, or guard the calling method with a cap.

trunkthumper.summary: This is a clear, idiomatic top-down domain: attackEnemy is a menu of plain strategies, doTrunkSlam uses a correct else ladder for variants, navigation uses pathNext recursion, and every operator is guarded. Its only weaknesses are essay-length comments and health/stamina arithmetic that is finer-grained than this game plans at.

findings.issue: This is an effect engine with its own ontology. The chain reacts(fire, rope, abyss) -> hazard(abyss, fallen) -> regionHas -> status(?e, fallen), with suffered/2 on top (part2.htn:12), skillElement, charge/3, unlimited and role/2, rebuilds 'chemistry' where the game's words would do. reacts/3 and hazard are named as slop in the rubric.
findings.fix: Use the game's words: enemy(ogre), ally(warden), terrain(bridge, rope), skillAppliesTag(ignite, fire), skillAppliesTag(gust, push), hasTag(?t, fallen). Delete the reacts/hazard/regionHas/suffered chain.

findings.issue: cutTheFloor (part4.htn) finds its place only through the chemistry chain. Its if() never says who holds fire, who can bring the target, or that two distinct allies act, so the feasibility is hidden in bringTo and castElement. Its do() is made of one-off helpers (bringOthers, stepOff, castElement) that no other strategy uses.
findings.fix: Write if(enemy(?t), terrain(?r, rope), skillAppliesTag(?s, fire), hasSkill(?a1, ?s), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)), then do(bringMobToLocation(?t, ?r), prepareToUseSkill(?a1, ?s, ?r), useSkillOnLocation(?a1, ?s, ?r)). Use the generic verbs that other strategies share.

findings.issue: bringAndPush (part3.htn) looks up the drop through hazard/regionHas/connected. It does not state who can push, or that the target is not immune. forceInto (part3.htn:21-22) has an empty if() and hides the immunity check in push. The lure method is a dead alternative: the comment itself says nothing is pulled into a drop.
findings.fix: Write if(enemy(?t), locationCanApplyTag(?l, fall), skillAppliesTag(?s, push), not(immune(?t, push)), hasSkill(?a, ?s)), then do(bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)). Remove the forceInto/lure layer.

findings.issue: The level encodes physics in the graph. The one-way connected(brink, void) and connected(ledge, void), the region() filter and 14 lineOfSight facts do this. It uses connected/2 instead of linked/2, so pathNext can't be used and navigation depends on a hand-written ladder in the deleted core.
findings.fix: Use linked/2 between regions only. Mark the edge as a location that applies the tag, e.g. locationCanApplyTag(brink, fall), and let the engine handle line of sight.

findings.issue: try(bringOthers(...)) inside the strategy for one enemy also moves the other enemies. That ties defeat(ogre) to defeat(bearer) through a side effect. allOf under try is all-or-nothing and commits once it succeeds, so the plan set depends on what order the search runs in.
findings.fix: Keep each strategy about its own ?t. Let the goal menu add a separate strategy that brings two targets onto the rope when that is the intended plan.

findings.issue: The charge/3 tokens (m1, d1, i1) and unlimited/1 are resource bookkeeping. skillElement(dash, dash) names a skill kind after the skill, although the comment says it is a taunt.
findings.fix: Use hasSkill plus skillAppliesTag(dash, taunt) and skillAppliesTag(magnetize, pull). If single use matters, model it as a tag the skill removes.

findings.issue: role(player, player) and role(warden, companion) set the player apart from the companions. Cooperation should come from the strategy's actor slots, not from roles.
findings.fix: Write ally(player). ally(warden). Have strategies bind distinct allies with \==(?a1, ?a2) in if().

findings.issue: Every file opens with an essay. There are 36 lines of level narrative, plan counts per kit, 'F4 strips these' and 'See design.md for the iterations', plus multi-paragraph headers in part2-part4.
findings.fix: Keep one header line per file and one line per method, e.g. '% Cut the floor: bring the target onto the rope, then burn it.'

the_brink.summary: The goal menu (defeat -> apply(?e, fall) with two plain alternatives) and the negated base case are the right shape. Everything below it is a chemistry/effect engine with coined vocabulary and one-off helpers, and the strategies' if() hides who acts and with what.
